q: Right-turns must be made from which lanes when travelling on a laned roadway?
options: The far right-hand lane or any other lane having an arrow pointing right.
The lane carrying the least amount of traffic.
The far left-hand lane.
explain: When travelling on a laned roadway, right turns must be made from the right-hand lane unless there are right-turning arrows in other lanes.

q: Which vehicle in the diagram must give way?
options: Vehicle J.
Vehicle K.
Vehicle L.
explain: At intersections where the road turns, watch to see who has the give way or stop sign to determine who has right-of-way. In the example below, the car at J must wait for the other cars.

q: You want to make a left turn. You must use your left-hand indicator -
options: At all times.
Only when there is traffic behind you.
Only when arrows are marked on the roadway.
explain: Turning left should be treated the same way as turning right. Always indicate. Be careful if you are overtaking a cyclist and want to turn left immediately after. Always check over your shoulder.

q: You wish to turn left here. The pedestrian lights are flashing red. You should -
options: Move into the right hand lane.
Give way to pedestrians still crossing.
Slowly move through the intersection turning left.
explain: Vehicles turning into that street must give way to pedestrians already crossing.

q: When these lights are flashing it means -
options: Pedestrians who have started crossing must go back to the footpath.
Pedestrians must not start to cross.
Pedestrians are not allowed in this area at this time.
explain: Pedestrians must not start to cross when the red man or 'Don't Walk' is shown, and they must not start to cross when the red man or 'Don't Walk' starts to flash.

q: A GIVE WAY sign at an intersection means that you must -
options: Be ready to stop and give way to all other traffic if there is danger of a collision.
Stop completely at all times and have no right of way.
Slow down and only give way to traffic on your right.
explain: Give way signs are placed at intersections where you can usually see far enough up the road to judge approaching traffic, as opposed to stop signs which are placed at intersections which have reduced visibility. You must still be prepared to stop, though.

q: You wish to go straight ahead at this roundabout. Which statement is true?
options: You must always leave the roundabout in the left lane.
You must enter in the right lane and leave in the left.
You must leave the roundabout in the same lane as you entered.
explain: When going straight ahead, approach the roundabout in any lane marked for going straight ahead and don't indicate. Only indicate left as you pass the exit before the one you want to take. Leave the roundabout in the same lane as the one you entered in.

q: When approaching a railway level crossing displaying this sign, you must -
options: Increase your speed to avoid any approaching trains.
Slow down, look both ways for trains and be prepared to stop if necessary.
Continue across at normal speed, do not slow down.
explain: Always be ready to stop in these situations, just in case you haven't seen the train coming.

q: You wish to turn left at this roundabout. Which lane may you use?
options: Either lane.
Right lane.
Left lane.
explain: The left-hand lane can be used for turning left or going straight ahead, whereas the right-hand lane can be used for turning right and going straight ahead.

q: You come to an intersection in Sydney with a Light Rail vehicle about to enter. What should you do?
options: Enter the intersection, but keep away from the Light Rail vehicle.
Wait until the intersection is clear.
Change lanes before crossing the intersection.
explain: If you come to an intersection with a Light Rail vehicle about to enter you must wait until the intersection is clear.

q: In this roundabout with two lanes, can the marked car turn right?
options: Yes, after changing to the right hand lane.
Yes, at any time.
No, not at any time.
explain: No, the left-hand lane can only be used for turning left or going straight ahead.

q: The diagram shows a marked pedestrian crossing at an intersection. There is also a STOP sign at the intersection. You have already stopped for a pedestrian. Must you stop again at the STOP line?
options: Yes, at all times.
Yes, if there is traffic on your right only.
No, if the intersection is clear.
explain: The diagram below shows a marked pedestrian crossing at an intersection. There is also a STOP sign at the intersection. Even if you have already stopped for a pedestrian you must stop again at the STOP line.

q: When there are no arrows marked on the road, left turns must be made from -
options: The far left-hand side of the road.
The middle of the road.
Either side of the road.
explain: You should leave room for other vehicles to pass on your right.

q: What should you do on approaching a railway level crossing displaying a STOP sign?
options: Slow down to 10 km/h, then proceed through the crossing.
Stop at all times and proceed when safe to do so.
Stop, only if a train is at the crossing.
explain: When there's a STOP sign it is compulsory to stop even if you think you can see the way is clear.

q: The traffic on the other side of this intersection has stopped. You are in the car shown and want to cross the intersection. The lights are green. What should you do?
options: Drive through the intersection slowly and hope that it will clear before the lights change.
Wait until there is enough room for your vehicle to cross the intersection completely.
Drive into the intersection and then turn left.
explain: When you come to an intersection and the road beyond is choked with vehicles going in the same direction you must wait until there is room to completely cross the intersection, even if your traffic light turns green.

q: When you wish to turn left at a roundabout you indicate -
options: Left only after you enter the roundabout.
Only if you think it necessary.
Left from start to finish.
explain: You should start indicating as you approach the roundabout and only stop indicating once you have made your turn.

q: If turning at an intersection are you required to give way to pedestrians?
options: Yes, a driver turning right or left must give way to pedestrians, if there is a danger of a collision
Yes, only if turning left.
Yes, only if turning right.
explain: You must also give way if you are turning and they are crossing the road. You must also give way even if there is no marked crossing if you are in danger of colliding with them.

q: You wish to make a right-hand turn from a ONE WAY STREET with no arrows marked on the roadway. You should position your vehicle -
options: On the right-hand side of the street.
In the middle of the street.
On the left-hand side of the street.
explain: You should leave room for other vehicles to pass on your left.

q: If turning right at a T-intersection (as shown) must you give way to vehicles approaching from both the left and right?
options: Yes, whether they are turning or not.
No, only the vehicle on the right.
No, you have right of way.
explain: If you are turning right at a T-intersection from the bottom of the T, then you must give way to your left and right to vehicles crossing the top of the T.

q: If the boomgates are down and the signals are flashing, at a railway level crossing, you may begin to cross -
options: If you cannot see a train approaching.
Only when the gate is up and the lights stop flashing.
If you can safely go around the closed gate.
explain: If there are boom gates down and flashing red lights then you must stop, and you must not cross the railway until the lights have stopped flashing and the boom gates have lifted.

q: You are in car A and are going straight ahead through the intersection. Who should give way?
options: Car A.
Whoever gets to the intersection first.
Car B.
explain: You have the right of way over cars entering from the left. Car B should give way.

q: Even if the signal at a railway level crossing does not indicate that a train is coming, you should -
options: Speed up and cross the tracks quickly.
Slow down, be ready to stop and give way if there is danger of collision.
Stop completely at all times.
explain: Always be ready to stop in these situations, just in case you haven't seen the train coming or the signal is not working.

q: When you wish to drive straight ahead at a roundabout you may enter from either the left or right lane. As you continue around you should -
options: Change lanes to get through quickly.
Move into another lane with least traffic.
Keep in the lane you entered the roundabout.
explain: When going straight ahead, approach the roundabout in any lane marked for going straight ahead and don't indicate. Only indicate left as you pass the exit before the one you want to take. Leave the roundabout in the same lane as the one you entered in.

q: In this diagram both vehicles O and P must pass through GIVE WAY signs before entering the intersection. Which vehicle goes first?
options: Vehicle P
Vehicle O
It depends on who moves first.
explain: When you are facing another vehicle at a crossroads, if you are turning right you must wait for any vehicles coming straight through or turning left. Therefore in the diagram, vehicle P has right of way over vehicle O.

q: You are in car A and want to turn right at this intersection. Car B facing you is also indicating to turn right. What path should you take?
options: Choose either depending on the traffic.
Pass behind each other.
Both pass in front of each other.
explain: If both vehicles are turning right then they don't need to cross each other's paths. They can pass in front of one another at the same time.

q: You are driving the car in the diagram. You must stop -
options: Only if there is a car on your right or left.
Even when there is no other traffic.
Only if there is danger of a collision with another vehicle.
explain: When there's a STOP sign it is compulsory to stop even if you think you can see the way is clear.

q: You approach an intersection in busy traffic and want to go straight ahead. The traffic lights turn green. When are you permitted to enter the intersection?
options: Immediately after the traffic lights turn green.
Only when there is room for your vehicle on the other side.
When the vehicle behind signals you to go.
explain: When you come to an intersection and the road beyond is choked with vehicles going in the same direction you must wait until there is room to completely cross the intersection, even if your traffic light turns green.

q: The motorcyclist wants to travel straight ahead through this roundabout. The rider should watch out for the marked car because the car -
options: May stop suddenly.
Could be going too fast.
May be leaving the roundabout.
explain: The motorbike should be cautious about the car on the roundabout as it could be leaving the roundabout and therefore cut across in front of the motorcyclist.

q: As you approach an intersection, you should check for traffic on your left and right -
options: At all times before entering the intersection.
Only when the traffic is heavy.
Only when you approach a stop sign.
explain: As you approach an intersection you should check for traffic on your left and right at all times. If it's a crossroads, look for traffic coming towards you that might turn right in front of you. Pay particular attention as cyclists and motorcyclists are more difficult to see at intersections because of their smaller profile. Look twice in case you missed something on your first glance.

q: You drive up to an intersection with a stop sign. There is no painted stop line. Where should you stop?
options: At least five metres before the intersection.
Before coming to and as near to the intersection as possible.
At the point where you can see clearly in both directions.
explain: You should stop as close to the intersection as possible.

q: Which statement is correct?
options: Red light cameras take photographs of vehicles that speed through intersections.
Red light cameras take photographs of vehicles that enter intersections when the lights are red.
Red light cameras take photographs of vehicles that cross intersections when the lights are yellow.
explain: The camera only takes a photo if you cross the stop line more than 0.3 seconds after the light has gone red. This means that if you have already entered the intersection on a yellow light, it won't trigger the camera.

q: As you drive into an intersection, the lights turn to yellow. You should -
options: Accelerate as hard as you can.
Continue through the intersection.
Brake immediately to a stop.
explain: As the lights have only just turned yellow there should be enough time for you to make it through the intersection before the lights turn green for other traffic.

q: To turn back into the same road from which you joined this roundabout you must -
options: Use the left lane all the way round.
Move into the left lane to leave the roundabout.
Stay in the right lane all the way round.
explain: If you want to travel completely around the roundabout it's like an extended right-hand turn. Simply keep the right signal on until you've passed the exit before you want to exit the roundabout, then exit into the right-hand lane, like in this diagram.

q: If a STOP or GIVE WAY sign has been knocked down, for example, as the result of an accident, does the line marked across the road have any meaning?
options: Yes, it has the same meaning as the sign itself.
No, but you must give way if turning.
No, you only need to give way to the vehicle on your right.
explain: If a STOP or GIVE WAY sign has been knocked down, for example, as the result of an accident, the line marked across the road indicates the meaning of the sign, and must be obeyed.

q: You are in the right hand lane and are planning to go straight ahead through this roundabout. When should you signal left to exit the roundabout?
options: At point M.
At point N.
At point O.
explain: If you want to go straight ahead at the roundabout you would signal left as you pass point O.

q: Vehicle O is at a STOP sign -
options: Vehicle O must give way to vehicles P, Q and R.
Vehicle O must give way only to vehicle R.
All vehicles must give way to vehicle O.
explain: Vehicle at a STOP sign have the lowest priority of all other signs at an intersection. In the example below, vehicle O must wait for all other vehicles to complete their manoeuvres.

q: You drive up to an intersection with a stop sign in the car marked A and you wish to turn right. The car marked B facing you also has a stop sign and is indicating to turn left. Who can go first?
options: Car A.
Car B.
Whoever arrives at the intersection first.
explain: If both opposing vehicles have the same class of sign, e.g. two stop signs or two give way signs, then the give way rules apply. The vehicle turning left has right of way.

q: When turning left at a roundabout you should enter and leave the roundabout -
options: In the lane with least traffic.
In the right lane.
In the left lane.
explain: When turning left, approach the roundabout in the left lane indicating left and continue indicating while you make the turn. Exit the roundabout in the left lane.

q: When police officers are at intersections giving directions you must -
options: Wait for the traffic lights to start working again.
Drive through the intersection as you normally would.
Always follow any instruction they give you.
explain: Instructions from a police officer override signs and lights at an intersection. If there is a traffic controller in the intersection you must obey what they tell you.

q: This intersection does not have any traffic lights or signs. You are in car A and want to turn right. When can you go?
options: Before the car going straight ahead has passed.
After the car going straight ahead has passed.
As soon as you get to the intersection.
explain: When you are turning, you give way to vehicles coming from straight ahead.

q: When you come to an intersection and the road beyond is choked with vehicles going in the same direction, what should you do?
options: Wait until there is room for you to completely cross the intersection.
Proceed if there is no traffic on your right.
Travel into the intersection and wait until traffic ahead moves.
explain: When you come to an intersection and the road beyond is choked with vehicles going in the same direction you must wait until there is room to completely cross the intersection, even if your traffic light turns green.

q: You are at an intersection and see a pedestrian crossing the road into which you are turning. You must -
options: Swerve around the pedestrian to avoid hitting them.
Sound your horn to warn the pedestrian to get out of the way.
Give way to the pedestrian.
explain: Vehicles turning into that street must give way to pedestrians already crossing.

q: At this intersection there are no signs or traffic lights. You are in the car marked A. You want to turn left. What should you do?
options: Enter the intersection and make the turn.
Slow down and give way to car B on your right.
Sound the horn to warn the other driver.
explain: If you are turning left at a T-intersection from the bottom of the T, then you must give way to your right to vehicles crossing the top of the T.

q: When making a right-hand turn at the intersection shown, you must give way to -
options: An oncoming vehicle going straight ahead or turning left and any vehicle on your right.
A vehicle approaching from your left and intending to turn right.
Only pedestrians.
explain: If you are at an unmarked crossroads and you are turning right then you must give way to any vehicle coming from straight ahead and turning left, and any vehicle coming from the right that's going straight ahead or turning right.

q: You want to turn left at this roundabout. Which lane must you use?
options: Either lane.
Lane B.
Lane A.
explain: When turning left, approach the roundabout in the left lane indicating left and continue indicating while you make the turn. Exit the roundabout in the left lane.

q: If both vehicles P and O in the diagram are turning right, which vehicle is in the best position to turn left into the street marked "X"?
options: Vehicle O.
Vehicle P.
Neither vehicle.
explain: When travelling on a laned roadway, right turns must be made from the right-hand lane unless there are right-turning arrows in other lanes. The left-hand lane traffic can also turn right. Any vehicle wanting to turn into the road at X would use the left hand lane.

q: You are at a busy intersection with slow moving traffic and want to go straight ahead. When the traffic lights change to green you should make sure that -
options: You have the car in the right gear.
You do not block the intersection.
You do not hold up the traffic behind you.
explain: When you come to an intersection and the road beyond is choked with vehicles going in the same direction you must wait until there is room to completely cross the intersection, even if your traffic light turns green.

q: If you enter an intersection that is under the control of a traffic controller -
options: Stop at the intersection and then proceed slowly.
Sound your horn at the traffic controller and hope they get out of your way.
Follow the directions of the controller.
explain: Instructions from a traffic controller override signs and lights at an intersection. If there is a traffic controller in the intersection you must obey what they tell you.

q: You wish to go straight ahead on this roundabout with two lanes. Which lane may you use?
options: Right lane only.
Left lane only.
Either lane.
explain: When going straight ahead, approach the roundabout in any lane marked for going straight ahead.

q: It is important to scan while driving so you can see everything that is happening on the road. What does scanning involve?
options: Looking further ahead down the road when driving.
Looking in the rear and side mirrors continually when driving.
Continually looking ahead, to the sides and using all mirrors when driving.
explain: Continually scanning in all directions keeps you aware of the situation all around you and gives you a better chance of reacting to emergency situations.

q: You should leave a gap between your vehicle and the one you are following. In good conditions the gap should be -
options: 1 second.
2 seconds.
3 seconds.
explain: Three seconds is a safe distance that gives you time to react and stop in an emergency situation.

q: Many people crash within the first few years of driving. What is the best way of learning to drive on your own without crashing?
options: Drive in every kind of traffic situation as soon as you get your licence.
Drive as much as you can with friends on the way to parties.
Start driving in daylight where it is not too busy and only drive in busier traffic as your driving gets better.
explain: Driving and riding experience is gained over time. Build up your skills on familiar roads in daylight and light traffic. Progress to heavier traffic and unfamiliar roads once you are confident in your driving ability.

q: It is night time and you are driving home from the movies. You are travelling in a line of vehicles. What size gap should you leave between your vehicle and the vehicles in front of you?
options: The same 3-second gap you would leave during the day.
A gap of about 2 seconds so you can watch the vehicles in front closely and see when they are stopping.
A gap of about 4 seconds as it is easy to misjudge distances at night.
explain: At night it is more difficult to judge distances and speeds so you should leave a longer gap behind the vehicle in front.

q: At night, if an oncoming vehicle's headlights dazzle you, you should -
options: Slow down, until your eyes recover.
Watch the centre line of the road.
Close your eyes for a short time until they recover.
explain: If you are dazzled, look at the left of the road, slow down and stop if necessary until your eyes recover.

q: When it is very foggy during the day or night and your vehicle has no fog lights, you should -
options: Put on your high beam lights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights and hazard warning lights to make your vehicle seen.
Follow closer to other vehicles.
explain: Fog is worse to drive in if you have your headlights on high beam, so slow down and use your low beam headlights.

q: Under good conditions, when driving behind any vehicle, at any speed, you should -
options: Stay at least three seconds behind the vehicle in front of you.
Drive as close to the vehicle in front as possible.
Stay one second behind the vehicle in front of you.
explain: Staying three seconds or more behind the vehicle in front will give you time to react in an emergency. If the conditions are wet, then you should increase this distance.

q: Why should you avoid heavy braking on a wet road?
options: If the wheels lock up your handbrake may not work.
Your wheels may skid and cause a loss of control.
You might wet pedestrians walking along the footpath.
explain: When you are driving on wet surfaces you have less grip overall and your vehicle may skid under heavy braking. Once you are skidding you are out of control.

q: When driving in wet weather, your vehicle will -
options: Take longer and further to stop, so slow down.
Stop in the same distance as on a dry road.
Handle better, so you can go faster.
explain: If it starts to rain the roads can become very slippery as the layer of grime and oil on the surface will mix with water, therefore you should allow for longer stopping distances.

q: While driving, you come across aggressive, selfish or ignorant driving behaviour by another driver. You should -
options: Stop your vehicle and call the police
Respond by using your horn and/or flashing your lights to let the driver know how you feel.
Stay calm and in control of your vehicle at all times.
explain: Remember that you are the one in control of the car, not your passengers, and you have a responsibility to be safe on the roads. Don't give in to peer pressure.

q: What is the best way to avoid hitting other vehicles, people or animals when moving off from the kerb?
options: Have a good look around while you walk up to your car and then drive off as soon as you can.
Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before moving off from the kerb.
Sound your horn before moving away from the kerb to warn people of your intentions.
explain: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see if a vehicle or a cyclist is coming.

q: When driving on a slippery wet road, for example, one covered in early morning dew, your vehicle will -
options: Take longer and further to stop.
Be heavier to steer.
Be easier to steer and handle.
explain: There is less friction on the road when it is wet, therefore you should allow for longer stopping distances.

q: At night, when you approach an oncoming vehicle, you should -
options: Carefully watch the vehicle by looking directly at its headlights.
Not look at its headlights, but keep left and watch the left of the road.
Put your lights on high beam, to make your vehicle more easily seen.
explain: Avoid looking at the headlights of oncoming vehicles because it will cause your pupils to contract and make you less able to see hazards. Looking at the left of the road will allow you to judge where you are without being dazzled by the oncoming vehicle's lights.

q: At night you should -
options: Use your hazard warning lights when overtaking another vehicle.
Leave a longer gap behind the vehicle in front.
Drive closer to the vehicle in front so they can see you better.
explain: At night it is more difficult to judge distances and speeds so you should leave a longer gap behind the vehicle in front.

q: If you are driving and it starts to rain, you should -
options: Slow down using the brake gently, since rain and oil may create a slippery surface.
Put your lights on high beam so you can see better.
Put your hazard warning lights on and increase your speed to avoid the rain.
explain: Be especially careful when braking as oil and rain create a very slippery surface. Slow down to give yourself time to react, and also to allow for safe cornering and stopping.

q: If you are a new driver and first start to drive at night you should -
options: Drive long distances to improve your concentration.
Drive mainly in unfamiliar streets.
Drive mainly on streets that you know well.
explain: At night it is more difficult to judge distances and speeds. Build up your skills on familiar roads when you start driving at night.

q: You set out on a fairly long drive to see some friends. After a while you start feeling tired. What should you do?
options: Make sure you get plenty of fresh air circulating inside the car by winding down your window.
Stop at a shop and get a drink that contains caffeine to help keep you awake.
Pull off the road, stop and rest until you no longer feel tired.
explain: Find a suitable place to pull up, take a break and just sleep for 10-15 minutes. Wait for another 10 minutes before setting off driving again, and take a short walk to get your blood flowing. If you have another driver, let them drive and then you can take a nap in the passenger seat.

q: You are planning to drive from Sydney to the Gold Coast with some friends. To minimise fatigue and make the trip as safe as possible you should -
options: Aim to drive for as long as possible when you are feeling good so you can arrive earlier.
Drive mostly at night as there is less traffic on the road and therefore less risk of crashing.
Drive during the day, take plenty of breaks and share driving if possible.
explain: Take regular breaks and swap drivers is possible.

q: You are about to move away from the kerb in your car. What is the last thing you should do before you move into traffic?
options: Adjust your seat.
Check over your shoulder.
Put on your seat belt.
explain: The last thing you should do is check in your blind spot over your right shoulder in case another vehicle or a cyclist is coming.

q: Which of the following attitudes is most likely to make you a safer driver?
options: It is up to other drivers to avoid crashing into me.
When I drive, I have the main responsibility for my safety and the safety of other road users.
Crashing or not crashing is a matter of luck.
explain: Remember that you are the one in control of the car. You are the responsible person for your driving and the safety of others as a result of your driving.

q: When going on a long trip, out of the following which is the most important to do?
options: Make sure your horn is working.
Get plenty of rest before starting out.
Have a good meal before driving.
explain: The only way to be not tired when you are driving is to have a good rest beforehand, or to have a short nap by taking a break, finding a suitable place to pull up and just sleeping for 10-15 minutes.

q: If you get sleepy while driving, it is best to -
options: Stop, rest, and change drivers if possible.
Turn on the radio very loud.
Turn on the air conditioning or open the windows.
explain: Turning up the radio and opening the windows have negligible effect on tiredness. Stopping and resting until you are not tired, or changing drivers is the best solution.

q: You are driving an older relative for an appointment and are running late. They ask you to go faster to get there on time. You should -
options: Drop them off at the train station.
Take the advice of a more experience driver and go faster where you can.
Choose a safe speed and say you will not go any faster.
explain: Remember that you are the one in control of the car, not your passengers, and you have a responsibility to be safe on the roads. Don't give in to peer pressure.

q: In wet weather when it becomes hard for you to see, you should -
options: Turn on your headlights, slow down, and double your following distance behind the vehicle in front.
Turn your headlights on high beam.
Flash your headlights to warn other drivers.
explain: Your stopping distances will increase in the wet, and if visibility is impaired it may take you longer to react to an emergency situation. Other vehicles will not be able to see you as easily, therefore headlights are important.

q: If you take medicine and then drink alcohol -
options: It can have a particularly bad effect on your driving ability.
The alcohol will have less effect than if taken alone.
Your ability to react to emergencies will improve.
explain: Consuming alcohol alongside medications can lead to an increased risk of drowsiness and other side effects. You should also check with your doctor that it is safe to drive when taking a specific medication.

q: Is it an offence to refuse to take a POLICE breath test?
options: Yes, always.
No, if you say you haven't been drinking alcohol.
No, if you are a learner driver.
explain: It's always an offence to refuse a police breath test. If you are convicted of driving with a blood alcohol level above the limit you will be fined, you will lose your licence and you could be sent to prison.

q: If you are going out and going to drink alcohol, the best way to avoid having to drink and drive is to -
options: After you have had a few drinks, start to think about how you will get home.
Organise before hand a way of getting home where you are not the driver.
Wait for one hour after your last drink before you drive home.
explain: Organise a taxi, a dedicated driver that doesn't drink, or take public transport to get home.

q: If you are taking several medications and you want to drive, you should -
options: Ask your passengers to let you know if you are not driving as well as you should.
Ask your doctor if the combination of drugs will make it dangerous to drive.
Drive carefully around your local streets to see if you are affected.
explain: Prescription drugs need the advice of a doctor or pharmacist before you take them, and they may have unwanted side effects that affect your ability to control a vehicle.

q: Before taking any drugs and then driving it is most important to -
options: Have some food in your stomach.
Plan to have some other person with you.
Know what the effects of the drug are.
explain: Your doctor or pharmacist will advise you of any potential side effects of your medication.

q: If you are driving a bus, taxi, hire-car, heavy motor vehicle (over 13.9 tonnes Gross Vehicle Mass), or a vehicle with a dangerous load, it is an offence when the level of alcohol in your blood reaches -
explain: The level is 0.02 for drivers of vehicles with a GVM greater than 13.9 tonnes, or carrying dangerous goods, or carrying paying passengers. This means there is 0.02 grams of alcohol in every 100ml of blood.

q: Having 1 or 2 alcoholic drinks before driving -
options: Improves your driving ability.
Will affect your reactions and judgement.
Has no effect on your driving ability.
explain: It is always safest to not have a drink at all before you drive as any amount of alcohol impairs your ability to drive.

q: If you are affected by a legal drug, such as a medicine (e.g. cold or allergy tablets) -
options: You may drive only in daylight hours.
You must not drive.
You must have a passenger to help you drive.
explain: Medications can make you drowsy and less able to judge situations on the road. Do not drive if you feel affected.

q: Alcohol is a depressant. This means -
options: It speeds your brain up so you can work better.
It slows down how quickly your brain works.
It makes you calm down and think more clearly.
explain: Alcohol is a depressant which means it slows down your ability for your brain to work. Alcohol will slow down your reaction times.

q: What is the safest way to stay under the legal alcohol limit?
options: Exercising and drinking black coffee.
Buying a breathalyser (alcohol measuring instrument).
Not drinking any alcohol.
explain: It is always safest to not have a drink at all before you drive as any amount of alcohol impairs your ability to drive.

q: After drinking alcohol you could -
options: Be able to drive the same as you normally can.
Misjudge speed (your own and others).
Be able to pay close attention to details in the traffic.
explain: Alcohol will slow down your reaction times. It gives you more confidence, but less ability. It makes it easier for you to misjudge other drivers' speed and direction, and for you to judge what speed you are approaching obstacles on the road.

q: When drivers have been drinking, the crashes they are involved in are generally -
options: Less serious.
About the same.
More serious.
explain: Your likelihood of having an accident increases because your control over your vehicle decreases the more you drink, and the more drunk you are the more likely you are to engage in riskier driving such as speeding.

q: If you have used illegal drugs you -
options: Must not drive.
Should drink coffee before driving.
May drive only in light traffic.
explain: All illegal drugs have dangerous effects on your body and affect your ability to concentrate or make rational decisions. Do not drive if you have used illegal drugs.

q: On Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights, how many serious crashes involve alcohol?
options: About 10%.
About 30%.
About 50%.
explain: On Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights the proportion of serious injury crashes involving alcohol rises to about 50% - it's the leading cause of serious vehicle accidents.

q: If you are taking any sort of medicine, you should -
options: Only drive a motor car not a heavy vehicle.
Only drive during the day after taking the medicine or drug.
Find out from your doctor or chemist whether the medicine or drug will affect your driving and act accordingly.
explain: Your doctor will be able to tell you which medications will affect your driving and, if driving is necessary for you, they might be able to change your diet or exercise regime to reduce your need for a specific medication (e.g. for blood pressure), adjust the dose, adjust when you take your medication, or change the medicine to one that has different effects that don't effect your driving.

q: Before driving a motor vehicle or riding a motor cycle it is safest -
options: Not to drink any alcohol.
Drink 1 nip of spirits (30 ml or 1 oz).
Drink 1 middy (285 ml) of light (low alcohol) beer.
explain: It is always safest to not have a drink at all before you drive as any amount of alcohol impairs your ability to drive. Alcohol is a depressant which means it slows down your ability for your brain to work.

q: When you are driving on a two-lane freeway, which lane should you choose?
options: The right lane to avoid slow-moving vehicles
Whichever lane has the least traffic
The left lane unless you are overtaking
explain: Unless you are overtaking another vehicle you should drive in the left hand lane to ensure the best traffic flow.

q: You are driving in a 60 km/h zone, with only one lane for traffic in your direction. You see a bus ahead (with this sign displayed on the rear) signalling its intention to pull out from a bus stop, you should
options: Sound your horn to stop the bus from pulling out
Slow down, and give way to the bus as it has priority
Continue at your normal speed as the bus does not have priority
explain: You must allow the bus to move into your lane. Also, be aware that passengers (especially children) may be trying to cross the road, so be prepared to stop.

q: Are you permitted to park on a median strip or traffic island?
options: No, not at any time
Yes, in daylight hours
Yes, but for no more than 30 minutes
explain: The median strip is only to be used to allow vehicles to safely turn into a side road without impeding the flow of traffic, or to enter traffic flow safely from a side road.

q: You are about to make a right hand turn at this intersection. You have the green light. You hear a siren and then see that a fire truck will soon overtake you. You should
options: Speed up to beat the fire truck
Continue and make the turn because you have the right of way
Stop and let the fire truck overtake you
explain: Stop and allow the fire truck to negotiate its way around you, minimising the chance of an accident. Be careful as there could be multiple emergency vehicles.

q: If you hold a learner or provisional licence class what is the Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) limit?
options: Zero.
explain: You must not drink any alcohol and drive on a learner or provisional licence. This is because alcohol affects reaction times and learner and P-plate drivers already have to cope with many situations they may not be familiar or comfortable with, and that take their entire concentration.

q: When you see the headlights flashing on the front of a bus, what should you do?
options: Stop and wait for the lights to stop flashing
Drive past the bus only while the lights are flashing
Be careful, there may be children about
explain: It's compulsory to drive no faster than 40 km/h past this because it's a school bus dropping off or picking up children. They keep flashing for about 30 seconds after the door closes and continue even after the bus moves off. This is to warn you that children might be crossing.

q: What is meant by this sign on or near a bridge?
options: Slow down and be prepared to give way to vehicles travelling in the opposite direction
Stop at all times before crossing the bridge and only give way to pedestrians who may be crossing
Do not overtake a vehicle travelling in the same direction
explain: When you approach a narrow bridge or a narrow road with a 'Give way' sign, you must slow down and prepare to stop. You must give way to vehicles approaching from the opposite direction as the road may not be wide enough for two vehicles.

q: Looking at the diagrams, how far from the approach side of a bus stop or a railway crossing are you allowed to stand or park your vehicle?
options: At least 5 metres
At least 50 metres
At least 20 metres
explain: You must not park on a railway level crossing or within 20m before and 20m after it and within 20m before and 10m after a bus stop.

q: Are you allowed to use a hand-held mobile phone while driving a car?
options: Yes, but you must hold the steering wheel with at least one hand
Yes, but only when you stop at intersections
No
explain: It is illegal to use a hand-held phone while you are driving. Heavy fines apply.

q: You want to park your vehicle for a short time. It is night time. You should
options: Leave your headlights on high beam
Park on the footpath
Pick a visible position or leave the parking or hazard lights on
explain: When parking at night you should ensure that your vehicle is as visible as possible. If you think that visibility isn't that good, put your hazard warning lights on.

q: Can a P1 or P2 provisional driver legally instruct a learner driver?
options: No
Yes, provided the provisional driver has held a P2 licence for more than 6 months
Yes, provided L and P1 or P2 plates are displayed
explain: P1 and P2 drivers are not yet experienced enough behind the wheel to legally instruct a learner driver. To supervise a learner, you must hold a current full Australian driver licence. Both a supervisor and a learner driver can be fined if the supervisor does not have a full Australian licence.

q: You hear the siren of an ambulance approaching you from behind. You should
options: Continue at the same speed
Slow down to the speed of other traffic
Move into the left lane
explain: Pull over to the left to give the emergency vehicle as much space as possible to overtake you. Don't brake heavily. Emergency services drivers are trained not to pressure a driver into doing something dangerous and will find a way through.

q: Is it an offence to obstruct clear vision of your number plates?
options: No, you are allowed to cover your number plates if you want to
Yes, but it is legal for a tow-bar or bicycle rack to cover the rear number plate
Yes, at any time
explain: It is an offence for drivers and registered operators of vehicles if its number plates are not fitted properly, obscured, defaced or otherwise not legible. You need auxiliary plates if the caravan, trailer, bike rack or vehicle you're towing covers your rear number plate.

q: To drive safely, you need to concentrate and be able to monitor everything that is happening on the road. To do this, you need to
options: Ask other occupants in the vehicle to watch out for possible dangers
Turn all your attention only to the road ahead
Continually scan the road, looking ahead, to the sides, checking side and rear mirrors and anticipate what may happen
explain: Scanning is where you look ahead, to the sides and in your mirrors so that you build a picture of where other vehicles are, what hazards are ahead and where your potential exit routes are if you need to take evasive action.

q: Are you permitted to drive a car towing more than one trailer?
options: No, not at all
Yes, if the combined length of vehicle and trailers does not exceed 15 metres
Yes, provided you have held a licence for two years
explain: Cars are not designed to cope with pulling multiple trailers, and loss of control could occur.

q: If a vehicle you are driving is involved in an accident and a person is injured, what must you do after stopping?
options: Only call the Police if the accident also resulted in over $500 worth of property damage
Render every assistance and take immediate steps to have an ambulance notified then call the Police
Report the accident to Police within seven days
explain: The first priority is to help injured people. If you're involved in a crash that causes death or injury and you do not stop and help, you can get a fine and be sent to prison.

q: What are you required to do if you develop a serious medical condition that could affect your driving?
options: Hand your licence in at the nearest police station
Once you become aware of the condition you must notify the TfNSW
Tell your doctor and let him or her notify the TfNSW
explain: You must notify Transport for NSW of a medical condition or recent surgery affecting your ability to drive safely. Your doctor is not responsible for notifying them.

q: Where there are double dividing lines, you may park
options: At least two metres from the dividing lines
At least three metres from the dividing lines
One metre from the dividing lines
explain: You are not allowed to park within three metres of any double centre lines.

q: You have a six year old child with you in your car. You have just parked so you can collect a prescription from the chemist. You should
options: Leave the child in the car
Take the child with you
Ask an older person sitting nearby to watch the child
explain: Parked cars can get dangerously hot even on cool days. Never leave children or animals unattended in a car.

q: You have just passed this sign. Can you park on this road?
options: Yes
No, not at any time
Yes, but only in daylight hours
explain: You are not allowed to park on a motorway.

q: Where there is parallel kerbside parking, are you allowed to double-park alongside a parked vehicle?
options: No, not at any time
Yes, if delivering goods
Yes, if not obstructing traffic
explain: Double parking obstructs the road way and causes a hazard for other road users. Where there is parallel kerbside parking, you are not allowed to double-park alongside a parked vehicle.

q: If you are involved in an accident where your vehicle needs to be towed away and the Police does not attend the crash scene, you
options: Do not need to report the accident to the Police
Must report the accident to the Police Station nearest to where the accident happened within 24 hours
Only need to report the accident to the Police if someone was injured
explain: If police do not attend the crash scene, you must report the crash as soon as possible (within 24 hours).

q: If you are driving through a road work zone in the left hand lane and you see this sign you should
options: Stop and wait for directions
Speed up to get in front of any cars traveling in the right hand lane
Merge to the right and give way to other traffic
explain: Prepare to move to the right and to merge right like a zip (alternate vehicles). If traffic is heavy then it's likely that it will either be backed up, or it will be starting to back up, so check that traffic ahead of you hasn't stopped suddenly.

q: If one or two of your wheels run off the edge of the roadway, you should
options: Slow down gradually and ease back onto the road
Slow down quickly by braking hard
Increase your speed and drive back on the road
explain: Gentle inputs to the throttle and steering will minimise your chances of losing control.

q: You hold an unrestricted licence and are driving at 100 km/h in the country and pass this sign. What should you do?
options: You can continue to drive at 100 km/h if there are fences to stop farm animals from getting on the road
Slow down to a speed that will allow you to stop to avoid crashing into farm animals on the road
For the next 5 kilometres you must not exceed 60 km/h unless you pass an end farm animals speed limit sign
explain: If you come across farm animals on the road and a farmer is present, slow down, be prepared to stop. Animals are unpredictable and can cross the road at anytime.

q: If there are no lanes marked on the road, you should drive
options: Near to the lefthand side of the road
Anywhere on your side of the road
Along the middle of the road
explain: When driving on any road that does not have marked lanes you must keep your vehicle as near as practicable to the far left side of the road but be careful you're not driving on loose stones or debris that could puncture your tyre.

q: Your car registration expires today. You have your car inspected for registration renewal but it fails the inspection. What should you do?
options: You have seven days to have the car repaired, after which the TfNSW considers it to be unregistered
After today you must not drive the car until it has been repaired, passed another inspection and registered
Go to the TfNSW and ask them to renew your registration and tell them you will soon get the car fixed
explain: It is an offence to drive an unregistered vehicle on the road. You are only allowed to drive an unregistered vehicle for getting repairs, insurance or registration using the most direct route.

q: You buy a car and find that the spare tyre is smooth; the tread is only just visible. If you get a puncture will it be legal to drive the car with a smooth spare tyre?
options: Yes, but you must get the puncture fixed within 24 hours
No, it's illegal to drive a car with a smooth tyre even if it is the spare
Yes, if the tyre is correctly inflated and the side walls of the tyre are in good condition
explain: Smooth tyres have very little grip when the roads are wet and are dangerous to drive with, even if it's a spare tyre.

q: Before getting out of your vehicle you must
options: Check your headlights are turned off
Check your seatbelt is back in place Check your headlights are turned off
Check your mirrors and blind spots for pedestrians, bicycles or other vehicles
explain: Opening a vehicle door presents a significant danger to cyclists, as well as other vehicle users. Always check your mirrors and over your shoulder before opening your door.

q: How close can you park to another vehicle when parked parallel to the kerb?
options: You must leave at least 1 metre front and back
You must leave at least 2 metres from the front only
You must leave at least 3 metres front and back
explain: When you park parallel to the kerb you must leave at least one metre front and back for other vehicles to be able to exit their park safely. Where there is kerbside parallel parking you are not allowed to double-park alongside a parked vehicle as you will be obstructing the roadway.

q: You are driving at night with your headlights on high beam. When should you dip your headlights?
options: When within 200 metres of the vehicle ahead or an oncoming one
When within 200 metres of an oncoming vehicle only
Never, you are allowed to drive with your lights on high beam at all times
explain: Headlights on high-beam enable you to see further. However, headlights on high-beam may dazzle an oncoming driver so you must 'dip' them to low-beam when another vehicle is within 200 metres. You must also dip your high-beam headlights when driving within 200 metres behind another vehicle.

q: When driving at sunset or dawn on a dark day, what should you do?
options: Turn on your lights on low beam
Keep your sunglasses on to cut down headlight glare
Turn on your hazard warning lights
explain: Turning on your lights will make you more visible to other road users. However, keep them on low beam so you do not dazzle other drivers.

q: Do bicycle riders have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers and motorcycle riders?
options: No, they must give way to cars at all times when riding on the road
No, they must always ride on the footpath
Yes
explain: Bicycle riders have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers and motorcycle riders. Drivers must watch out for bicycle riders, as they are smaller than cars and harder to see. Also, they do not have the protection that drivers in cars, vans and trucks have.

q: Are you permitted to park in the direction of the arrow?
options: Yes, provided no taxis are using the area
Yes, if you are carrying two or more passengers
No, not at any time
explain: You must not stop in the direction of the arrow or arrows on the sign, unless driving a taxi. Some taxi zones have times shown. You can stop or park your vehicle outside those times.

q: You see a broken yellow line painted on the roadway adjacent to the kerb. What does it mean?
options: You may at any time, park along this part of the road for 1 hour only
Clearway restrictions apply you must not stop during the clearway hours
Bicycle riders must ride along the yellow line
explain: Clearways are designed to help traffic flow smoothly in busier times.

q: You are driving at night and there is no other traffic around you. When can you use your headlights on high beam?
options: Only on roads that do not have street lights
On any road where the speed limit is above 80 km/h
On any road, even if there are street lights
explain: You can use your full beam headlights even if there are streetlights, but be courteous to road users other than cars, such as cyclists and pedestrians.

q: If there are no signs or markings to advise you, can you choose any of these methods of parking?
options: Yes M, N and O are all legal
No, only N is correct
Yes, N is best but M and O are quite legal
explain: If there are no lines marked on the road (and assuming you are allowed to park there), then parallel parking applies, not angle parking.

q: You are driving your vehicle along a street and want to stop for a short time. Are you allowed to double park your vehicle (that is stand it on the road alongside a parked car)?
options: Yes, provided you stop for a short time only and turn on your hazard warning lights
Yes, provided you do not leave the vehicle
No, never
explain: Double parking obstructs the road way and causes a hazard for other road users. Where there is parallel kerbside parking, you are not allowed to double-park alongside a parked vehicle.

q: A friend lends you a van that has seats for ten passengers. What type of licence do you need to drive this type of vehicle?
options: A heavy rigid vehicle licence
A car licence
A small bus licence
explain: You can drive a van that will carry up to 12 people including the driver on a car licence.

q: You should be particularly careful at this intersection because
options: It looks a bit tricky
Intersections cause crashes
The building blocks a good view of the side street
explain: Buildings or trees can restrict your view of intersections. Slow down and pay extra attention.

q: Before driving on a freeway, which of the following should you do?
options: Make sure your vehicle has enough fuel, oil, water and the correct tyre pressure
Take your street directory in case you get lost
Take something to calm your nerves before driving
explain: Before driving on a freeway, make sure your vehicle has enough fuel, oil and water and the correct tyre pressure. It is important to have the correct tyre pressure because freeway speeds are high and incorrect tyre pressure can affect handling and increase the risk of a tyre blowout.

q: When merging onto the freeway from the entrance, you should
options: Sound your horn, turn on your indicator lights and move onto the freeway
Look for a large enough break in the traffic and adjust your speed so as to fit into the traffic flow
Stop and check the traffic behind you on the entrance
explain: Match your speed and merge into a gap in the traffic. Trying to merge into freeway traffic too slowly causes a dangerous situation for other drivers who may have to brake heavily.

q: Where must L or P plates be displayed on a vehicle
options: Anywhere inside the windows but only if they are not tinted
Anywhere including on the dashboard
On the front and back of the exterior of the vehicle
explain: The plates must be displayed on the front and back of the exterior of the vehicle and not be obscured.

q: If you intend to turn left, are you required to give a signal?
options: Yes, if turn signals are fitted to your vehicle
No, if turning left from a lane marked left turn only
No, if arrows are marked on the roadway
explain: Even if there are arrows marking a left turn, you must signal to avoid ambiguity for other drivers.

q: You should use your right-hand indicator when
options: You intend to slow down
You intend to move to the right, at any time
You are about to stop
explain: Get in the habit of using your indicator every time you make a manoeuvre as it tells other drivers what your intentions are, even if it's the only way you can turn.

q: This bridge has only just enough room for two vehicles. As you come close to it you should
options: Slow down and pay extra attention
Maintain your speed, keeping to the limit
Sound your horn to warn the other driver
explain: If you are driving towards a narrow bridge slow down especially if wider vehicles are coming.

q: Before driving a long distance at fast speed or carrying a full car load, you should
options: Check your tyre pressure, and if necessary, increase it to what the manufacturer recommends
Make sure you have a street directory, so you know where you are going
Have a large meal and a cup of coffee
explain: Before driving a long distance, it is important to have the correct tyre pressure because incorrect tyre pressure can affect handling and increase the risk of a tyre blowout.

q: You are in busy traffic and slow down for a bicycle rider. A driver behind you beeps a horn and pressures you to go around the bike and drive faster. How should you respond?
options: Go slower because the slower you go the safer you are
Overtake the bike quickly and speed up to stop the other driver becoming aggressive
Resist the pressure, stay calm and overtake the cyclist when it is safe
explain: You are in control and other drivers' impatience should not influence your decisions to act safely. Only overtake when it is safe for the cyclist and yourself to do so.

q: Stop signs or flashing lights at railway crossings should always be obeyed, because
options: Pedestrians might be crossing
Trains are fast, heavy and cannot stop quickly
Car brakes often fail
explain: Stop signals at railway crossings should be obeyed because trains are fast and heavy and cannot stop quickly or deviate from the tracks. Check for trains even if the lights are not flashing.

q: When reversing, you should
options: Take care and never reverse for a greater distance and time than is necessary
Unbuckle your seat belt so you can reverse as quickly as possible
Sound your horn to warn other drivers
explain: Always check your mirrors and over your shoulder before reversing. It's more difficult to control your vehicle when reversing than driving forwards, so you should never reverse for any more distance than is necessary.

q: If you see a sign indicating road repairs are going on, you should
options: Stop immediately and wait for instructions
Slow down and watch for traffic controllers and instructions
Maintain the same speed
explain: When approaching roadworks, slow down for the safety of workers, look out for any hazards and be prepared to stop if instructed to.

q: If an oncoming vehicle crosses the centre line and is coming straight at you and you cannot stop, you should
options: Slow down and hope that the driver will turn away
Brake, look for room to the left, sound your horn and flash your lights
Drive onto the wrong side of the road and hope the other vehicle does not do the same
explain: The more speed you can scrub off, and the further you are to your left, the more chance you have of avoiding an accident, or at least minimising its effects. Never try to dodge by pulling right. They may suddenly realise the predicament and instinctively swerve back into the proper lane, colliding with you.

q: You are driving along this road. You hear an ambulance's siren and see the ambulance in your mirror. You should
options: Move to the right and make way for the ambulance
Turn into a driveway on the right hand side of the road
Move to the left and make way for the ambulance
explain: Pull over to the left to give the emergency vehicle as much space as possible to overtake you. Don't brake heavily. Emergency services drivers are trained not to pressure a driver into doing something dangerous and will find a way through.

q: When you come across roadworks
options: You only have to obey the signs during working hours
You only have to obey the signs when there are workers about
You must obey the signs that are displayed at all times
explain: When approaching roadworks, slow down, look out for any hazards and be prepared to stop. You must obey the regulatory signs and traffic lights at roadworks. Look out for road workers on the road and obey signals from traffic controllers.

q: When displaying L or P plates, how much of the letter must be clearly visible?
options: Most of the letter
Only enough of the letter so it is clear whether it is an L or P
All of the letter L or P
explain: The plates must be displayed on the front and back of the exterior of the vehicle and not be obscured. None of the letter must be hidden.

q: You are driving on a freeway and realise you forgot something at home. You want to go back for it. Can you do a U-turn on this road?
options: Yes, any time
No, not at any time
Yes, providing you use the gravel joining roads
explain: If you forgot something, continue driving and take the next exit. Make your way back to your desired exit on the other side of the freeway.

q: You are turning right from one of two right turn only lanes. How should you use your indicators?
options: You should not indicate at all because it might confuse other drivers
Indicate with your right hand signal the same as any other right hand turn
Indicating in this situation is optional Give a right hand signal if you think it will help other road users
explain: Whenever you perform a right hand turn to change lanes or at an intersection you must use your right hand signal, even if that's the only way you can turn.

q: What must you do when you are towing a caravan to help other vehicles overtake?
options: Keep at least 60 metres behind heavy vehicles or other vehicles towing caravans
Drive at least 25 km/h below the speed limit
Stop immediately and let the faster vehicle overtake
explain: You should leave a gap of at least 60 metres, so other vehicles overtaking you can pull in safely after overtaking you, gradually leap-frogging the line of slower vehicles.

q: You should not drive across a railway level crossing when
options: You are towing a caravan
Traffic is blocking the other side
A station is nearby
explain: If traffic is blocking the other side you may get stranded on the tracks. You must not drive onto a level crossing while a train is approaching or if the road on the other side of the crossing is blocked.

q: You should angle park
options: Where there is plenty of room from the centre line
Where there are markings or a sign indicating angle park
Where the road is very wide
explain: If there are angle park markings, that is how you should park. If there are no lines marked on the road, then parallel parking applies.

q: Do you have any responsibilities when opening a vehicle door on a roadway?
options: Yes, you must not open a door if you are likely to cause danger to road users or impede traffic
No, any following traffic must stop if the door interferes with its progress
No, there is no regulation to cover this situation
explain: Opening a vehicle door presents a significant danger to cyclists, as well as other vehicle users. Always check your mirrors and over your shoulder before opening your door.

q: The red car wants to turn right and exit the roundabout in the street indicated by an arrow. Is the car positioned in the correct lane to do this?
options: Yes, the car can make the turn from either the left hand or the right hand lane.
Yes, the car can make the turn only from this lane.
No, the car should enter the roundabout only from the right hand lane.
explain: The red car is not in the right position to turn right at the roundabout because is in the left-hand lane.

q: At the T-intersection shown in the diagram which vehicle should give way?
options: Vehicle R.
Vehicle Q.
Whichever vehicle got there last.
explain: At an unmarked T-intersection, even if someone is turning in front of you, you must wait for them if you are on the bottom of the T.

q: To reduce the effect of alcohol before driving or riding you should -
options: Wait. The time depends on how much you have drunk.
Drink black coffee.
Have a glass of water.
explain: The only way to get your blood alcohol down is to wait. Adding other liquid does not affect your body's ability to eliminate the alcohol.

q: You want to drive your car but you have a very bad headache. A friend gives you some of their headache tablets to kill the pain. What should you do before you take these tablets?
options: Ask your friend if the tablets have affected them.
Read the label and confirm they are not prescription drugs and there are no special warnings on the label.
Drink a large glass of milk because this reduces the adverse effects of medicines and drugs.
explain: Prescription drugs need the advice of a doctor or pharmacist before you take them, and they may have unwanted side effects that affect your ability to control a vehicle.

q: You are going to a party where everyone is drinking alcohol. What can you do to lower the risk of being in an alcohol related crash on the way home?
options: Get a taxi or other public transport there and back, or organise for someone to pick you up.
Take your car, try not to drink too much alcohol and then drive home.
Organise a lift home with someone from the party.
explain: If there is no dedicated driver that doesn't drink, organise a taxi, someone to pick you up, or take public transport to get home.

q: Even if you feel unaffected after drinking alcohol, you should -
options: Drive, but avoid using freeways.
Be aware that your abilities are decreased.
Spend more time than usual looking in the mirrors.
explain: Any amount of alcohol impairs your ability to drive. Alcohol is a depressant which means it slows down your ability for your brain to work.

q: You want to leave your automatic car parked on a street sloping uphill. You should
options: Park only on flat areas
Put the handbrake on and put the transmission in 'P' (park)
Turn the wheels away from the kerb
explain: In an automatic car you should put the gearbox in 'P' (park) and put the handbrake on. You can also turn your wheels towards the kerb for added security as if the car rolls it will turn itself towards the kerb.

q: When you see these lights flashing on the back of a bus, what should you do?
options: Stop and wait for the lights to stop flashing
Overtake the bus only while the lights are flashing
Drive carefully at no more than 40 km/h
explain: It's compulsory to drive no faster than 40 km/h past this because it's a school bus dropping off or picking up children. They keep flashing for about 30 seconds after the door closes and continue even after the bus moves off. This is to warn you that children might be crossing.

q: To progress to a P2 provisional licence, a P1 provisional driver must hold a P1 licence for a minimum period of
options: 12 months
18 months
24 months
explain: You have to hold a P1 licence (red Ps) for at least 12 months before you can attempt the Hazard Perception Test in order to proceed to your P2 licence (green Ps). Your P1 licence is valid for 18 months, if you don't apply for your green Ps during that time.

q: Bicycle and motorcycle riders have the same rights to use the road as other motor vehicle drivers. They are, however, more at risk in traffic because
options: They ride too fast and do not turn their lights on
They are careless and do not obey road rules
They are harder to see in traffic and do not have the same protection as many drivers
explain: They are smaller and less visible. Also, they do not have the protection that drivers in cars, vans and trucks have.

q: If your vehicle is involved in an accident (regardless of the damage), what details must you give, to the other driver(s), if asked?
options: No details at all until you have contacted your insurance company
You must let them see your licence, take details, and give the name and address of the vehicle's owner
Only your name and address details if a Police officer asks for them
explain: If you're involved in a crash you must give the other person or people involved your name and address, your vehicle registration number or the name and address of the owner of the vehicle, if you're not the owner.

q: If you are driving towards a road works zone and a traffic controller displays a stop sign you must
options: Slow down and continue through the road works zone
Stop and then proceed if you think it is safe
Stop your vehicle and follow the directions of the traffic controller
explain: The traffic controller will let you know when it's safe to pass through the road works. There might be vehicles coming the other way, or workers or machinery blocking the lane.

q: Are you required to carry your driver's licence with you every time you drive?
options: No, being licensed is enough
No it is only needed on long trips
Yes
explain: You must carry your drivers licence with you at all times when you drive. If you are stopped by the police and you do not have your licence on you, you will be given an on-the-spot fine or summonsed to court.

q: You are approaching a green light in vehicle A. An ambulance sounding its siren is approaching the same intersection and has a red light. You should
options: Pull over to the left before you reach the intersection
Keep driving because you have the green light
Slow down and stop if necessary to prevent getting in its way
explain: Wait at the intersection until the ambulance negotiates its way around you, minimising the chance of an accident. Be careful as there could be multiple emergency vehicles.

q: You drive up to a corner where you see some loose gravel on the road. You should
options: Speed up and drive over the gravel as quickly as possible
Check the mirrors and change lanes
Slow down
explain: The gravel acts like ball bearings under your wheel. Slow down and avoid braking heavily.

q: When there are three lanes on a freeway
options: The right lane is for avoiding most traffic
The right lane is for emergency vehicles only
The right lane is reserved for overtaking
explain: The usual driving lane is the left-hand lane on a freeway. Only use the right hand lane and middle lane for overtaking.

q: Are you permitted to tow a caravan with a person riding in the caravan?
options: No, not under any circumstances
Yes, provided you do not exceed 60 km/h
Yes, if the person(s) in the caravan are over 12 years of age
explain: Caravans are not designed to be crash-proof. A person in an accident in a caravan is likely to be seriously injured or worse.

q: As you leave a freeway, which of the following should you check?
options: Your speed
Fuel gauge
Windscreen wipers
explain: Travelling at freeway speeds is deceptive. If you are coming to an intersection, roundabout or zone with a lower speed limit, begin to slow down early and adjust your speed appropriately.

q: Which side mirror is adjusted best?
options: Mirror A
Mirror B
Mirror C
explain: Mirror A allows you to see back up the lane as far as possible and while minimising your blind spot.

q: When can a private car travel in a lane marked by this sign?
options: Only within 100 metres of making a turn
When carrying at least two passengers
Only to overtake another vehicle
explain: Private vehicles can drive in bus lanes to avoid an obstruction or if there's a sign saying they can. They can also drive in a bus lane for a maximum of 100m to enter or leave the road.

q: You borrow a friend's car and find that the position of the driver's seat puts you sitting a long way from the steering wheel and controls. What should you do?
options: Put up with the discomfort; you should not adjust another person's seat
Adjust the seat forward so it's right for you
Ask your friend for a cushion to place behind your back
explain: Put the seat in a position where you can reach the steering wheel with slightly bent arms and reach the pedals.

q: Generally, if you hear the siren of an emergency vehicle you should
options: Let the emergency vehicle pass and follow it closely behind
Immediately come to a stop
Pull over to the left until the emergency vehicle passes
explain: Pull over to the left to give the emergency vehicle as much space as possible to overtake you. Don't brake heavily. Emergency services drivers are trained not to pressure a driver into doing something dangerous and will find a way through.

q: What must you do if you miss your exit on a freeway?
options: Continue until you reach the next appropriate exit
Stop, and reverse back along the freeway to the exit you missed
Stop immediately and turn around
explain: If you miss your exit, continue driving and take the next exit. Make your way back to your desired exit on the other side of the freeway. Reversing on the freeway is dangerous and prohibited.

q: If you see a horse and rider on the road what should you do?
options: Sound your horn to warn the rider
Slow down and give them plenty of room
Speed up to pass the horse
explain: If you're passing a horse, whether it's being ridden or led, or is pulling a vehicle, you should slow down and give them plenty of space. Horses can be frightened easily by traffic and can become unpredictable.

q: You change lanes and then see you are in a lane where the T3 rule applies. There is no other traffic in this lane. You have one passenger. What should you do?
options: Keep driving in the T3 lane because there is no other traffic in it.
Change lanes as soon as it is safe because you are not permitted to travel in a T3 lane with only two people in your car.
Immediately pull over to the left and stop. Then wait until it is safe to continue in another lane.
explain: As you only have two people in your vehicle you cannot travel in the T3 lane. T3 lane must have a driver and at least two other occupants.

q: Which movements shown in the diagram can legally be made by the driver of the purple car?
options: O, P and Q.
O and P only.
P only.
explain: The road has a double line, but the purple car's side is a broken line therefore it's possible to overtake another vehicle as well as turn into a driveway or side street.

q: You are in car marked A. You wish to overtake car marked B. You should -
options: Cross the unbroken single line and overtake.
Wait behind car B until it moves into the left lane.
Cross the line and overtake only if it is safe.
explain: Wait until car B has completed its overtaking manoeuvre. Do not cross the unbroken single line.

q: Which movements shown in the diagram can legally be made by the driver of the purple car?
options: O and P only.
P only.
O, P and Q.
explain: The road in has a double unbroken dividing line therefore the purple car can only cross it to turn into a driveway (assuming it's safe to do so), not to overtake another vehicle. The line is broken where there is a side street so it can turn into it.

q: It is early morning and there is no other traffic about. You approach an intersection when the traffic lights change from green to yellow. What should you do?
options: Keep going.
Stop.
Drive through and sound your horn.
explain: You should always stop when the lights turn yellow unless stopping abruptly would cause an accident.

q: When two lanes merge into one (as shown in the diagram), who should give way?
options: The vehicle which has to cross the lane line.
The faster vehicle.
The vehicle in the right-hand lane because it is overtaking.
explain: When two roads merge into one road, the vehicle that has to cross the lane line must give way.

q: You are facing traffic lights (as shown). What do they mean?
options: You may proceed only in the direction of the green arrow.
You may proceed only in the direction of the green arrow when the red light has changed to green.
You must give way to oncoming traffic.
explain: On some intersections you will find a red turning arrow which means you can turn on a red light if the turning arrow is green. You must wait if there are any pedestrians crossing the road.

q: You are driving a car and want to pick up a passenger. The lane you want to stop in is a BUS LANE. Are you permitted to stop there?
options: Yes, if you pick the passenger up and then immediately drive off.
Yes, you are allowed to stop in a BUS LANE for as long as you like.
No, unless you are driving a hire car or a taxi.
explain: You must not drive in a bus lane if it is only reserved for buses unless you are driving a taxi or hire car.

q: Are you permitted to make a U-Turn at traffic lights?
options: No, unless there is a U-TURN PERMITTED sign at the intersection.
Yes, at all times.
Yes, if there is no danger of colliding with another vehicle.
explain: You must not make a u-turn at traffic lights unless there is a 'U-TURN PERMITTED' sign.

q: It is 3 o'clock in the morning. You cannot see any other traffic. You want to turn right. You may -
options: Turn right when you have waited one minute.
Not turn right while the arrow is red.
Turn right if it is safe to do so.
explain: Even if it's the middle of the night and there is no one coming, you must not go through a red light.

q: You approach an intersection showing a red light and the sign shown. You wish to turn left. You must -
options: Stop and turn left only if it is safe.
Slow down and turn left or right if it is safe.
Stop and wait for a green light.
explain: At some intersections with lights a left turn is permitted after stopping. Stop and turn left only if it is safe.

q: You wish to turn left at this intersection. The traffic lights are red and you see this sign. You should -
options: Stop until the light turns green.
Stop then go straight ahead.
Stop, then if you see it is safe turn left.
explain: You must stop first and only turn left if it is safe to do so.

q: You are waiting at an intersection and the lights are red. The traffic lights change to green. You should -
options: Cross the intersection as quickly as possible.
Check both sides of the intersection and then proceed.
Wait until the traffic behind you makes you move.
explain: You should check for traffic on your left and right at all times. Pay particular attention as cyclists and motorcyclists are more difficult to see at intersections because of their smaller profile.

q: When the road is marked this way are you permitted to cross the lines and overtake?
options: Yes.
No.
Yes, only if the way ahead is clear.
explain: There are double unbroken dividing lines which you are not permitted to cross to overtake, unless you are overtaking a cyclist.

q: You want to turn right at an intersection and see this traffic light. You should -
options: Move forward slowly.
Enter the intersection and wait for the green arrow.
Stay behind the stop line until the green arrow shows.
explain: You must not drive through a red light. Wait behind the line until the green arrow turns green.

q: When driving in traffic lanes (as shown in the diagram), you may change your lane -
options: Only when it is safe to do so.
Without looking, provided you use your indicator
Provided you sound your horn to warn other drivers
explain: Before changing lanes you must first check your mirrors, then signal your intentions, then check your mirrors and blind spot, then make the manoeuvre. Even if you can't see any other road users around you must still indicate for at least five seconds because there could be a motorcyclist, cyclist or other road user you haven't seen.

q: Looking at the diagram, which vehicle must give way?
options: Vehicle B.
Vehicle A.
Either vehicle, there is no rule on giving way when merging.
explain: If two lanes merge into one without a lane line, the vehicle that is ahead has right of way.

q: When starting to overtake you see the dividing lines ahead change to double unbroken lines. What should you do?
options: Continue to overtake because you started when the line was broken.
Do not overtake because you are not permitted to overtake on double lines.
Keep overtaking and cut in in front of the other car as soon as possible.
