explain: If you see the dividing lines are double unbroken ones then you must not overtake.

q: Overtaking another vehicle requires good concentration and judgement. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: It is best and safest to speed up when a vehicle behind you tries to overtake you.
The faster the vehicle you are overtaking is going, the less distance you need to overtake.
You need to watch out for all large, long vehicles which are turning.
explain: Large, long vehicles may unexpectedly turn across your path if you don't see their indicators.

q: Before changing lanes you should
options: Speed up so you are going faster than the traffic in the other lane.
Signal in plenty of time, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for other vehicles.
Signal for at least two seconds and quickly change lanes.
explain: If you don't signal in time other drivers may begin a manoeuvre which conflicts with yours, and if you don't look in your mirrors and over your shoulder you may not see a vehicle in your blind spot.

q: How should you merge with traffic when entering a freeway?
options: Watch for a gap and merge with the traffic at the speed it is travelling.
Speed up and force your way into the traffic.
Stop, then enter the traffic quickly.
explain: Watch for a suitable gap in the traffic and adjust your speed so that you arrive at the correct time. If traffic is heavy, merge alternately (like a zip).

q: This light means, you -
options: Must stop and wait for the red light before proceeding.
Can go straight ahead, or turn left or turn right, if it is safe to do so.
Can make a U turn provided it is safe to do so.
explain: A green light means you can turn left (if there are no crossing pedestrians), go straight ahead, and turn right (if you give way to traffic coming towards you).

q: Temporary traffic lights at road works -
options: Apply to road works vehicles only.
Are installed to warn motorists of construction works.
Must be obeyed.
explain: Temporary traffic lights are sometimes installed at roadworks and they should be treated as any other traffic light. The sign indicates where it is safe to stop.

q: Signalling is -
options: Not required when turning at T-intersections.
Not required when turning at traffic lights with a green arrow.
Always required before turning or lane changing.
explain: You must always signal when turning or changing lanes.

q: You drive into a transit lane where the T2 rule applies. You have one passenger plus yourself. Are you permitted to remain in the transit lane?
options: No, because you only have one passenger you must move out of the transit lane immediately.
Yes, you have two people in your car so you can drive in this lane.
Yes, you can remain in the transit lane, but only if you are turning left in 250 metres.
explain: As long as there are two or more people in your vehicle you can travel in the T2 lane. They must be real people, not pets or mannequins.

q: Double unbroken dividing lines are marked on a roadway. You may -
options: Cross them to turn into a driveway or property, if it is safe to do so.
Cross them to overtake a car ahead if it is safe to do so.
Cross them to make a U turn.
explain: You can only cross a double unbroken dividing lines to turn into a driveway (assuming it's safe to do so).

q: Which movements shown in the diagram can legally be made by the driver of the purple car?
options: O and P only.
P only.
O, P and Q.
explain: The road has a double line but the purple car is still allowed to cross it to turn into a driveway. The line is broken where there is a side street so it can turn into it. The purple car's side is an unbroken line therefore it's not possible to overtake another vehicle.

q: These lights mean that you -
options: Can turn left, but not go straight ahead.
Can turn left or go straight ahead.
Can turn left only if a sign "TURN LEFT AT ANY TIME WITH CARE" is displayed.
explain: Straight through traffic has a red light, therefore must stop. Traffic turning left can go if it's safe to do so.

q: How should you merge with traffic when entering a motorway?
options: Slow down and force your way into the traffic.
Stop, then enter the traffic quickly.
Watch for a gap and increase your speed to safely merge with the traffic.
explain: It's very important that you match your speed when merging so that you do not cause other traffic to brake. The reason for having an on-ramp or slip road is to allow vehicles to do this.

q: When driving on a multi-lane road with a speed limit of more than 80 km/h, which lane should you choose?
options: The right lane to avoid slow moving vehicles.
Either left or right lane.
The left lane unless overtaking.
explain: You should always use the left lane unless overtaking or you are about to turn right.

q: If you hear the siren of an emergency vehicle, you must -
options: Flash your headlights to warn other drivers.
Take whatever action is necessary (with safety) to make way for the emergency vehicle.
Increase your speed to avoid the vehicle.
explain: Usually moving to the left will allow the emergency vehicle to pass, but check in your mirrors to see where it is approaching from. If you are waiting at an intersection the ambulance driver will find a way through. Don't emerge into the intersection unless the ambulance waits behind you, and only emerge on a green light, not a red light.

q: At traffic lights what is meant when a red light appears?
options: Stop, wait behind the stop line until the lights change to green.
Stop, wait behind the stop line until the lights change to yellow.
Stop, make sure there is no traffic, then drive straight ahead.
explain: At red traffic lights you must stop if it's safe to do so then wait behind the line until the light turns green.

q: You are going to turn right from a one-way street. Where should you be when you start your turn?
options: Any position if it is safe to do so.
Position M. From the middle of the road.
Position R. As close as possible to the right side of the road.
explain: If there are no lanes marked on a one-way street and you want to turn right, make the right turn from the right-hand side of the road, as shown in diagram R. Positioning your car on the right allows other drivers to pass to your left.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: You are approaching a lane that is only for buses.
Slow down and prepare to stop for a train.
There is a lane just for light rail vehicles.
explain: Light rail vehicle lanes are marked with this sign.

q: You want to turn left at this intersection. There is an edge line that continues through the intersection. Are you permitted to turn here?
options: No, not under any circumstances.
Yes, you can cross an edge line to turn into or out of a street.
Yes, only if you are in a taxi, hire car, bus or you live in that street.
explain: You can cross an unbroken line to the left if it is to turn into an intersection.

q: What should you do when approaching traffic lights which change from green to yellow?
options: Stop at the stop line unless you are so close that sudden or sharp braking might cause an accident.
Speed up to clear the intersection before the lights change to red.
Stop, only if a red light camera is in use.
explain: Traffic light phases are set so that, at the speed limit, vehicles should be able to pull up safely when the light turns yellow without having to drive through the intersection while the light is red or make a sudden or sharp braking might cause an accident.

q: What may you do at an intersection with traffic lights at which this sign is displayed?
options: If the lights are red you must first stop, then you may turn left if it is safe to do so.
You should slow down and check if anyone is coming before turning left.
You may turn left only if a green arrow is shown.
explain: At some intersections with lights a left turn is permitted. You must first stop, check it's safe to proceed, then make a left turn.

q: You are in car marked Y and want to turn right using a median turning lane. A car marked O, coming towards you, is already in the median lane; it is slowing down and indicating. Are you permitted to enter and share the median turning lane?
options: No, if another car is already in the median turning lane you must not use it.
Yes, but only if you race the other car and get to the turning position first.
Yes, but you must be prepared to slow down and stop.
explain: You can enter the median strip, but be aware that the other vehicle must be able to complete its manoeuvre.

q: A section of road is marked with double unbroken dividing lines as in the diagram. When is a vehicle allowed to cross these lines?
options: To enter or leave a street or driveway.
To overtake a slow vehicle ahead.
When there is no traffic coming the other way.
explain: You can only cross a double unbroken dividing lines to turn into a driveway (assuming it's safe to do so).

q: As you approach an intersection with traffic lights, the yellow light turns to red. You must -
options: Speed up to avoid traffic from the left and right.
Stop and wait for the green light.
Sound your horn and proceed through the red light.
explain: At red traffic lights you must stop if it's safe to do so then wait behind the line until the light turns green. Red light cameras will trigger if you enter the intersection when the light is red.

q: You must use your indicator lights when -
options: Approaching a curve.
Changing lanes or turning left or right.
Double parking.
explain: You must use your indicators for all manoeuvres (pulling away from the kerb, overtaking a vehicle, merging, doing a u-turn, ...) and lane changes.

q: You wish to turn left at this intersection and the traffic lights are green. What should you do?
options: Move forward slowly, make the left turn and wait behind car A.
Enter the intersection and sound the horn.
Wait behind the stop line until there is room for you to enter the new road.
explain: When you come to an intersection and the road you want to go is choked with vehicles going in the same direction you must wait until there is room to completely cross the intersection, even if your traffic light turns green.

q: As you approach a set of traffic lights at an intersection, they change from green to yellow (amber). You must -
options: Drive through the intersection without accelerating.
Accelerate to clear the intersection before the lights change to red.
Stop before the lights, unless you are so close that sudden braking might cause an accident.
explain: You must stop for a yellow light unless doing so would cause an accident.

q: When you see these lights flashing on the back of a bus, what should you do?
options: Stop and wait for the lights to stop flashing
Overtake the bus only while the lights are flashing
Drive carefully at no more than 40 km/h
explain: It's compulsory to drive no faster than 40 km/h past this because it's a school bus dropping off or picking up children. They keep flashing for about 30 seconds after the door closes and continue even after the bus moves off. This is to warn you that children might be crossing.

q: Where do you stop at temporary traffic lights?
options: Where the lane ends.
After the traffic lights, but before the construction zone.
At the 'Stop here on red signal' sign.
explain: Temporary traffic lights are sometimes installed at roadworks and they should be treated as any other traffic light. The sign indicates where it is safe to stop. Also, some automated lights have a sensor for vehicles waiting at a red light so they know to turn the lights green again after a certain period of time. Parking forward of this sensor may mean the light does not change green.

q: A friend lends you his car. It is very noisy and blows a lot of smoke. He tells you the vehicle has been given a defect notice but it's still OK to drive it. What should you do?
options: Borrow the car, but always drive it 10 Km/h below the speed limit
Before you borrow the car check the defect notice to make sure it is legal to drive the car
Borrow the car but only drive on streets where the car will not be a danger to others
explain: A defect notice will be issued for a failed inspection and a vehicle will not pass a subsequent inspection until the necessary repairs specified on the defect notice have been fixed. In the case of a minor defect notice there will be a time period specified in which the defects must be fixed. For a major defect, the vehicle might be grounded.

q: If you are not sure you have enough distance to overtake a vehicle ahead, you should -
options: Wait for a better opportunity with more distance to overtake.
Put the vehicle in a lower gear and speed up.
Sound your horn to signal the driver ahead to slow down.
explain: Always be sure that you have enough time and distance to complete your overtaking move. If you are not certain, wait for a better opportunity.

q: The faster the vehicle in front of you is travelling, the -
options: More distance and time you need to overtake.
Less time you need to overtake.
Closer you must get before starting to overtake.
explain: You will cover more distance and need more time if the vehicle you are overtaking is going faster.

q: If the police suspect you may have been involved in street or drag racing, they may take immediate action. Which one of the following is correct? The police may -
options: Take your vehicle away and sell it at an auction.
Take your vehicle to the local police station and keep it till the following morning.
Take your vehicle from you and keep it stored for up to three months.
explain: For a serious driving offence like street racing, NSW police have the power to immediately impound the vehicle or confiscate its number plates for three months.

q: If you are convicted of driving with a blood alcohol level that is over the limit for your licence, you could lose your driver's licence. You may also -
options: Be restricted to driving an automatic vehicle.
Be sent to prison.
Have a personal speed limit imposed on you.
explain: Heavy fines apply for driving with excess blood alcohol. You also risk a disqualification and you may be sent to prison.

q: You are travelling in the left lane and wish to turn right at the intersection. You move to the right lane and a driver behind sounds their horn at you. What have you done wrong?
options: Driven too slowly.
Crossed an unbroken lane line.
Changed lanes unnecessarily.
explain: You are not permitted to cross an unbroken line unless you are turning into a driveway.

q: The speed limit on this road is 90 km/h. You have just overtaken a vehicle in the left lane. What should you do next?
options: Keep your position in this lane.
Move into the left lane.
Accelerate away from the other vehicle and keep driving in this lane.
explain: Once you have finished your overtaking you should move back into the left lane. If the road you are on has a speed limit of 80kph or more, or you've seen a keep left unless overtaking sign, you must drive in the left lane unless you're overtaking or want to turn right.

q: A driver behind you signals their intention to overtake your car. What should you do?
options: Keep to the left and let that driver overtake you.
Speed up so that the driver will not have to overtake.
Signal the driver to remain behind you if it is travelling too fast.
explain: Make it easy for the other person to overtake you by keeping left.

q: When you have started to overtake the car, you notice that its right indicator is flashing. You should -
options: Immediately brake to a stop.
Accelerate quickly to get past.
Check your mirror and move back in behind the car.
explain: Check your mirror so that you don't turn back in on another vehicle, then move back in behind the car.

q: When overtaking another vehicle you should NOT move back in front of it, unless -
options: You can see the overtaken vehicle in your rear vision mirror.
An oncoming car appears over a hill.
The driver of the vehicle signals it is safe to do so.
explain: Moving back into the left lane early may mean you hit the vehicle you are overtaking. It's particularly important if you are driving a longer vehicle to wait until you can see the overtaken vehicle clearly in your rear vision mirror.

q: When entering or leaving a driveway you must -
options: Blow your horn to warn other road users.
Stop and give way only to vehicles.
Give way to bicycles, vehicles and pedestrians.
explain: When exiting a driveway you must give way to bicycles, vehicles and pedestrians.

q: If you are convicted a second time for street or drag racing, which one of the following penalties applies?
options: You will not be able to register your vehicle again.
You will have to pay for the storage of your vehicle.
Your vehicle may be taken away and sold.
explain: For a second offence the vehicle could be confiscated permanently and sold or be used for crash testing by Transport for NSW (TfNSW). The maximum prison term is two years for a second or subsequent offence.

q: Before beginning to overtake another vehicle, you should -
options: Signal and slow down so you will have more room to overtake.
Check to see it is safe, change gear if necessary, and signal your intention before moving out.
Sound your horn, move out and overtake.
explain: An overtaking manoeuvre requires that you do several things: check it's safe to go, change gear if you are in a manual vehicle and will need the extra acceleration, and signal your intention for enough time. Be sure to check over your shoulder before you pull out to overtake in case a vehicle behind you has already started to overtake you.

q: You are driving behind a long vehicle (as shown) which has a sign saying DO NOT OVERTAKE TURNING VEHICLE. The long vehicle indicates that it is going to turn left. You -
options: May move to the left-hand side of the road and pass the long vehicle.
Must let the long vehicle turn first.
May pass the truck because it cannot turn left from the middle lane.
explain: Long vehicles may need to swing out wide to the right to make a left hand turn therefore you must not overtake it until it has made the turn.

q: You are approaching the crest (top of a hill) on a narrow road, the safest procedure is to -
options: Keep to the left and slow down.
Flash your headlights to warn oncoming traffic.
Increase your speed and sound your horn.
explain: Keeping to the left gives other vehicles more room, and slowing down ensures that if you reach the crest and see a previously hidden obstacle on the other side you have more time to stop.

q: If you are convicted of dangerous driving -
options: You could only be fined and given demerit points.
You could lose your licence and may be sent to prison.
You could be given demerit points only.
explain: You could lose your licence and you may be sent to prison. Around 50% of people that cause death through dangerous driving through excess speed end up in prison.

q: Another vehicle is overtaking you on your right. You commit a traffic offence if you -
options: Slow down while the other vehicle is on your right.
Keep the same speed.
Speed up while the other vehicle is on your right.
explain: If someone is overtaking you, keep to the left and let them overtake, and leave a space in front of you for them to pull back in. It's an offence to deliberately speed up to prevent someone from overtaking you.

q: On a single laned road (as shown), you must always overtake another vehicle on its right except when -
options: The other vehicle is turning right.
You are travelling at more than 80 km/h.
The other vehicle is going slower than you.
explain: You can overtake a vehicle on its left when it is waiting to turn right. You can also overtake on the left if you are travelling in marked lanes and the lane on the right is travelling slower than the lane on the left.

q: How should you overtake a pedal cyclist?
options: Drive as close as possible to the cyclist so he or she will move over and let you pass.
The same as you would another car, with safety.
Sound your horn to warn the cyclist to get off the road.
explain: Give the cyclist enough room when you overtake.

q: The speed limit on this road is 100 km/h. When can you use the right lane?
options: When there is no other traffic around.
Whenever you want to.
Only when overtaking or turning right.
explain: If the road you are on has a speed limit of 80kph or more, or you've seen a keep left unless overtaking sign, you must drive in the left lane unless you're overtaking or want to turn right.

q: When driving near parked vehicles, you should -
options: Check for parked vehicles with turn signals on, or children about to step out.
Stop, if you see a car with its right-hand indicator on.
Sound your horn and flash your headlights to warn drivers not to pull out.
explain: Parked vehicles maneouvring into traffic may not see you as they pull out. Children may also appear from behind parked vehicles. Be prepared to stop if required.

q: You are approaching a hill or curve. You must not cross the centre line to overtake -
options: If you do not have a clear view of any approaching traffic.
If you cannot see clear road ahead for 100 metres.
If you cannot see clear road ahead for 75 metres.
explain: Oncoming traffic could appear and you create the risk of a head-on collision.

q: If you have been convicted for street or drag racing, which of these penalties may apply?
options: You will be fined a small amount and get one demerit point.
You will be given a letter of warning and fined.
You will get three demerit points and a large fine.
explain: If you are found guilty of street racing you will automatically lose your licence for 12 months, but it could be for an unlimited period. The maximum fine is $3,300 and three demerit points.

q: If you are caught speeding through a road work zone you will -
options: Not receive any penalty as road works speed limits are only advisory.
Receive a warning letter in the mail.
Be liable for a speeding fine and loss of demerit points.
explain: At roadworks there will be road workers working on the road. Speeding vehicles can throw up stones, and also there's always the risk of hitting someone working there. Speeding through a road work zone is dangerous and you will receive a fine and demerit points.

q: When being overtaken by another vehicle what should you do to help?
options: Keep left and allow plenty of room to let the other vehicle back in.
Brake quickly to let the other vehicle overtake.
Move to the left and stop.
explain: Make it easy for the other person to overtake you, and leave space in front of you in case the overtaking vehicle needs to pull back into the line of traffic.

q: When driving through temporary road work you should -
options: Sound your horn.
Maintain current speed if the road is clear.
Slow down and look out for hazards.
explain: Road work zones have additional hazards. Slow down and be prepared for gravel, uneven road surfaces, obstructions, closed lanes, road workers, and heavy machinery that may be blocking a lane.

q: If an overtaking vehicle signals that it must move in, in front of you, you should -
options: Speed up and not let the vehicle back in.
Prepare to slow down to allow room.
Flash your lights at the overtaking vehicle.
explain: An overtaking vehicle may need to move in front of you if there is traffic coming the other way. Prepare to slow down if needed to avoid an accident.

q: Will a P1 licence be suspended for any speeding offence?
options: Only for 10 km/h or more over the speed limit.
No.
Yes.
explain: A P1 licence will be suspended for three months for any speeding offence.

q: The first thing you should do before overtaking is -
options: Sound your horn.
Make sure it is safe and the way is clear of oncoming traffic.
Increase your speed.
explain: You will need to make sure you have enough room to overtake, which is a function of the ability of your vehicle to get to the speed limit quickly, and how long it will take to pass the vehicle while doing the speed limit. You also need to check for solid lines on the road that mean no overtaking, and whether another vehicle has started to overtake you

q: What is this driver doing that is negligent and illegal?
options: Not signalling to change lanes.
Crossing an unbroken line at a curve.
Overtaking on the kerb side.
explain: The driver is cutting the corner and crossing the unbroken line. Even if the driver was signalling, this is still illegal because it's not for the purposes of turning into a driveway. Unbroken lines are there to warn drivers that the visibility of the road ahead is not sufficient to perform an overtaking manoeuvre.

q: You see these zig-zag markings on the road in front of you. What do they mean?
options: Look out for animals on the side of the road.
Take care and look out for pedestrians at a crossing.
Be careful because the road ahead is slippery.
explain: If there are zig-zag lines on the road before the crossing this means you're approaching a crossing with limited visibility, so take extra care.

q: Which sign painted on the road tells you there is a pedestrian crossing ahead?
options: B
A
C
explain: If there are zig-zag lines on the road before the crossing this means you're approaching a crossing with limited visibility, so take extra care.

q: At a pedestrian crossing with traffic lights, when the amber light starts "flashing" after the red stop signal, it means -
options: The traffic lights are out of order and pedestrians must not use the crossing.
You may carefully drive through the crossing, if there is no risk of colliding with pedestrians.
The green light is due. Do not proceed until the green light appears.
explain: At a pedestrian crossing with traffic lights, when the amber light starts 'flashing' after the red stop signal, it means you may carefully drive through the crossing, if there is no risk of colliding with pedestrians.

q: You must give way to pedestrians on a marked pedestrian crossing -
options: If there is any danger of a collision.
When they are crossing from your right only.
When they are crossing from your left only.
explain: Special markings on the road show where pedestrians have rights to cross and you must give way to them. You must also give way if you are turning and they are crossing the road. You must also give way even if there is no marked crossing if you are in danger of colliding with them.

q: Which statement is true?
options: Pedestrians have no special rights on the roads.
You must give way to pedestrians if there is any danger of hitting them.
You must give way to pedestrians only at marked crossings.
explain: You must also give way even if there is no marked crossing if you are in danger of colliding with them.

q: When approaching a marked pedestrian crossing and no pedestrians are in sight, you should -
options: Slow down and be ready to make a safe stop.
Come to a complete stop before the crossing.
Go faster, in case a pedestrian steps onto the crossing.
explain: Be aware that pedestrians can be obscured by signage and other vehicles and may step out in front of you. Slow down and be ready to make a safe stop.

q: When driving near pedestrian crossings, intersections, or school crossings, you should always -
options: Move into the left lane.
Slow down, watch for pedestrians and be ready to make a safe stop.
Keep your eyes on the speedometer.
explain: Always be on the lookout for pedestrians, especially children.

q: When you see older people on or near the road, you should -
options: Drive around them to keep the traffic moving.
Sound your horn and keep going at the same speed so you do not hold up the traffic.
Slow down and take extra care because they may not see you until you are very close.
explain: Older people may have impaired vision and hearing and this makes it more difficult for them to see your vehicle. Slow down and take extra care.

q: At a pedestrian crossing with traffic lights, when the lights change to red you should -
options: Slow down and give way to pedestrians.
Stop and continue after the pedestrians have crossed.
Stop, wait for pedestrians to cross and for the green light to come on.
explain: Once the green light comes on you can go, as long as there is no danger of you colliding with a pedestrian.

q: If you see a School Crossing Supervisor holding a sign like this, you must wait until the children -
options: Are off the crossing and the hand held sign is taken away.
Reach the right-hand side of the crossing.
Are out of sight.
explain: You must wait until the children are off the crossing and the hand-held sign is taken away.

q: When driving in wet weather, you should -
options: Drive in the middle of the road to avoid splashing pedestrians on the footpath.
Watch out for pedestrians, who may hurry and take risks.
Stop and help aged pedestrians across the road.
explain: They will often hurry when it's wet weather and their view might be partially obscured by an umbrella or raincoat hood.

q: These markings on the road indicate -
options: Places where you can park.
Places where pedestrians have special rights.
Places where special speed limits apply.
explain: Special markings on the road show where pedestrians have rights to cross and you must give way to them.

q: You must give way to pedestrians -
options: Only on marked foot crossings.
Only on marked foot crossings and traffic light pedestrian crossings.
At all times, if there is any danger of colliding with them, even if there is no marked crossing.
explain: You must also give way even if there is no marked crossing if you are in danger of colliding with them.

q: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Pedestrians must cross the road only at marked crossings and intersections.
You do not have to give way to adults crossing at children's crossings.
You must give way to pedestrians if there is a danger of a collision.
explain: Pedestrians will sometimes cross where there are no marked crossings. You must also give way even if there is no marked crossing if you are in danger of colliding with them.

q: When driving past parked vehicles, which of the following is it most important to do -
options: Drive in the right-hand lane, if there is one.
Watch for pedestrians, animals and car doors opening.
Stay as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
explain: Pedestrians and animals can be obscured by other vehicles. They may not see you and could try to cross in front of your vehicle. Also, do not drive too close to parked cars as there is a risk that someone opening a car door might hit your vehicle. However, you should still drive in the left hand lane unless turning right or overtaking.

q: This person is standing on a pedestrian refuge. If he steps out onto your lane you should -
options: Slow down and sound the horn to warn the person to move back.
Maintain your speed so you do not hold up the traffic.
Give way to the person if there is any danger of colliding.
explain: You must also give way even if there is no marked crossing if you are in danger of colliding with them.

q: You drive up to a Light Rail vehicle that has just stopped at a tram stop. What is the most important thing you should do?
options: Keep a look out for traffic coming in the opposite direction.
Slow down, but keep moving so you do not delay other drivers.
Take extra care, slow down and give way to the pedestrians.
explain: Pedestrians are generally looking for the shortest route and they will cross in front of and behind buses and light rail trams after they have got off, and anywhere where it's convenient rather than safe. Take extra care, slow down and give way to the pedestrians.

q: When driving in an area where there are many pedestrians (e.g. a bus stop) it is important to -
options: Put your headlights on high beam so they can see you better.
Slow down and watch for an indication that they will enter the road.
Increase your speed to avoid the chance of hitting them.
explain: Be aware that a bus can obscure pedestrians who may try to cross in front of your vehicle. Be prepared to stop if necessary.

q: Pedestrians who are affected by alcohol, are -
options: One of the most common groups involved in road accidents.
Unlikely to walk near the road and do not require your attention.
Less dangerous than sober pedestrians because they are more careful after drinking.
explain: Alcohol reduces a person's ability to judge distance and speed, therefore they are more likely to cross a road in front of a moving vehicle.

q: If elderly people or children are on a pedestrian crossing you will probably need to -
options: Wait extra time to allow them to cross safely.
Sound your horn to hurry them up.
Drive around them so you don't hold up traffic.
explain: Elderly, children and disabled people could need extra time to cross, so be patient.

q: A vehicle ahead of you has stopped at a pedestrian crossing. You -
options: Must not overtake the stopped vehicle.
May overtake the vehicle if there are no pedestrians on the crossing.
May overtake the vehicle provided no cars are coming the other way.
explain: If a vehicle has stopped at a pedestrian crossing you are not allowed to overtake it. Pedestrians may be obscured by the vehicle.

q: Which one of the following statements is correct? Bicycle riders -
options: Must obey the road rules.
May not travel on heavy traffic roads.
Must ride against the flow of traffic so they can be seen.
explain: Bicycle riders have the same rights as other road users and bikes are treated equally as vehicles.

q: When driving near children playing or walking near the edge of the road, you should -
options: Slow down, and be ready to make a safe stop.
Sound your horn to warn them of your presence.
Continue at the same speed and drive around them.
explain: Younger children and toddlers often have minimal road sense, yet are highly mobile. They can easily catch their parents off-guard and dash into the road after a ball, for example.

q: When you see children on or near the road -
options: You should reduce your speed by 5 km/h.
You should ignore them and pay attention to the rear vision mirror.
You should slow down and be more careful because they may move suddenly.
explain: Younger children and toddlers often have minimal road sense, yet are highly mobile. They can easily catch their parents off-guard and dash into the road after a ball, for example. Slow down and be prepared to stop.

q: You drive towards these people on the road. What should you do?
options: Continue at the same speed and sound the horn.
Stop and give way if there is any danger of hitting them.
Slow down until they are half way through the crossing and drive on.
explain: Special markings on the road show where pedestrians have rights to cross and you must give way to them.

q: You must give way to pedestrians if there is a risk of hitting them. When driving in poor light, you should -
options: Keep your headlights on high beam all the time.
Always drive in the right hand lane so you can be away from pedestrians.
Look more carefully for pedestrians because they are hard to see.
explain: Take care in the evenings and nights when they are not as easy to see.

q: You approach a crossing and see the scene in the picture. You should -
options: Slow down and drive through giving way to the children.
Stop and wait for the children until your lane is clear.
Slow down and stop until the supervisor takes down the sign.
explain: You must wait until the children are off the crossing and the hand-held sign is taken away.

q: You approach a person crossing the road. You should -
options: Slow down and sound your horn to hurry up the person.
Maintain your speed and swerve around the person.
Slow down or stop to avoid hitting the person.
explain: Special markings on the road show where pedestrians have rights to cross and you must give way to them.

q: Child restraints (eg, baby capsules and child seats) -
options: Are not as safe as holding a child in your arms.
Should be fitted according to the manufacturers' instructions.
Need only be used if the child wants to sleep.
explain: Children aged up to 7 years must be in an approved child restraint or booster seat suitable for their age and size - these must be fitted in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. They usually attach to ISOFIX points. Don't carry children in your arms (you won't be strong enough to hold in in a crash).

q: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Seat belts and child restraints are only required on short trips.
Occupants in a car fitted with airbags are not required to wear a seat belt.
By law, all occupants of a car (unless exempt) need to be restrained by a properly fitted and adjusted seat belt or a child restraint.
explain: When you take anyone in your vehicle it's important that you have enough seat belts for everyone. It's compulsory for all passengers to wear seat belts when they are fitted in the vehicle, unless they are exempt for medical reasons.

q: You give a friend and her 12 year old son a lift. Your friend sits in the front and her son gets in the back. The boy does not put his seat belt on. By law, who has to make sure the child wears his seat belt?
options: The child does because it is always the passenger's responsibility.
Your friend does because she is the parent.
You do, because you are the driver.
explain: Drivers are responsible for all passengers wearing a seat belt. Any passenger aged 16 or over who isn't using a seat belt where one is available will be fined along with the driver.

q: You want to fit a baby restraint to your car. What should you secure the restraint to?
options: Only at the back using the seat belt provided.
Any seat belt in the back or front of the car.
An anchorage point designed for a baby restraint.
explain: Children aged up to 7 years must be in an approved child restraint or booster seat suitable for their age and size - these must be fitted in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. They usually attach to ISOFIX points.

q: The adult passenger in the rear is breaking the law because he is -
options: Not wearing the available seat belt.
Sitting in the back seat.
Distracting the driver.
explain: It's compulsory for all passengers to wear seat belts when they are fitted in the vehicle, unless they are exempt for medical reasons. Drivers are responsible for all passengers wearing a seat belt.

q: Seat belts and child restraints (eg baby capsules and child seats) -
options: Are only needed on long trips.
Must always be worn properly, and adjusted tightly.
Are only needed on short trips.
explain: Seat belts and child restraints save lives and prevent injury. They are the most effective device for protecting passengers in an accident. They must always be worn properly and buckled tightly.

q: You want to give a lift to a friend and his four month old baby. Before you do, you need to make sure -
options: Your driver's licence permits you to carry children under the age of twelve months.
You have enough seat belts for all the passengers, including the baby.
You have a baby restraint properly fitted to your vehicle.
explain: Children aged up to 7 years must be in an approved child restraint or booster seat suitable for their age and size - these must be fitted in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions. They usually attach to ISOFIX points. Don't carry children in your arms (you won't be strong enough to hold in in a crash).

q: The most effective device for protecting passengers when in an accident is -
options: Seat belts.
Safety door latches.
Padded instrument panels.
explain: Seat belts save lives and prevent injury. They are the most effective device for protecting passengers in an accident. They must always be worn properly and buckled tightly.

q: When passengers get in the car and do not put their seat belts on, the safest thing to do is -
options: Say nothing because it's the passengers' responsibility to wear their seat belts.
Tell them the car has seat belts and they should wear them.
Drive slower than you normally would so the passengers are safe.
explain: Drivers are responsible for all passengers wearing a seat belt. Any passenger aged 16 or over who isn't using a seat belt where one is available will be fined along with the driver.

q: A car is carrying a driver and 3 adult passengers. There are seat belts in all seating positions. By law, seat belts must be worn by -
options: All four people.
Only the driver.
Only the driver and front seat passenger.
explain: It's compulsory for all passengers to wear seat belts when they are fitted in the vehicle, unless they are exempt for medical reasons. Drivers are responsible for all passengers wearing a seat belt.

q: You are driving a vehicle that only has a seat belt for the driver. To reduce the danger of being in a vehicle without a seat belt, where is the best place for passengers to sit?
options: In the front seat.
In the back seat.
In the front seat sharing your seat belt.
explain: If your vehicle doesn't have seat belts, the best place for passengers is in the back seat as it will give them the most protection.

q: Which one of the following statements is correct? Seat belts -
options: Save lives and prevent injury.
Do not have to be used in the rear seat.
Are not necessary for good drivers.
explain: Seat belts save lives and prevent injury. They are the most effective device for protecting passengers in an accident. They must always be worn properly and buckled tightly.

q: Having a radar detector or jammer in your car is against the law -
options: Only if it is turned on.
No matter what your reason is.
If you purchased it after 1998.
explain: A radar detector is a device installed in your grille or mounted on the inside of your windscreen which detects if your speed is being monitored by police using a radar gun. Jammers jam the signal from a police radar and they are illegal, too.

q: What could be the penalties for driving over the speed limit -
options: Fines only.
Fines, demerit points and possibly loss of licence.
A letter of warning and a small fine.
explain: You may receive a substantial fine, lose your licence and incur demerit points for exceeding the speed limit.

q: A Shared Traffic Zone, where pedestrians and other road users can share the road safely has a speed limit of -
options: 10 Km/h.
20 Km/h.
50 Km/h.
explain: Pedestrians will be using the road along with vehicles, therefore the speed limit is low. 10kph is the limit in shared zones including car parks and reserves.

q: You are driving in busy traffic in an 80 km/h zone. It begins to rain lightly. What should you do?
options: Slow down to a speed that suits the conditions better.
Keep going at the same speed because that's how fast the signs tell you to drive.
Pull over and wait till it stops raining.
explain: If there was a prolonged period of sunny weather before the rain then the surface can become very slick, especially with only light rain where there's not enough water to help wash the surface oil and dirt away quickly. Slow down to a speed that suits the conditions better.

q: You are driving in a 70 km/h zone, keeping to the limit. Several vehicles pass you. One of your passengers suggests you should keep up with the other traffic. What should you do?
options: Decide your speed yourself, based on the speed limit and the conditions.
Follow the suggestions and keep up with the traffic.
Speed up to a little bit over the speed limit, because everyone does it.
explain: Remember that you are the one in control of the car, not your passengers, and you have a responsibility to be safe on the roads. Don't give in to peer pressure.

q: This sign means you must -
options: Drive at 10 km/h if there are pedestrians around.
Reduce your speed to what you think is safe but never below 10 km/h.
Share this road with other people and vehicles and not exceed 10 km/h.
explain: You will be sharing this road with pedestrians and other vehicles. The speed limit is 10 km/h as shown by the speed limit sign.

q: You are driving in busy traffic in a 60 km/h zone. You feel 60 km/h is a bit too fast for the conditions. What should you do?
options: Keep up with the other traffic because it's probably safe if the sign says 60 km/h.
Slow down to a speed that suits the conditions.
Turn off the busy street and wait for traffic to clear.
explain: Remember that you are the one in control of the car and you have a responsibility to be safe on the roads. Don't give in to peer pressure. If you don't feel comfortable doing a certain speed, slow down.

q: If you are driving along the highway and come across road works with a reduced speed zone, you must -
options: Drive through the road works zone as fast as you can to get past it.
Drive at the same speed as other vehicles.
Slow down to the new speed limit.
explain: The reduced speed zone is to ensure the safety of any road workers, and also because road conditions might be slippery or damaging to your vehicle at higher speeds.

q: When you see this sign you must -
options: Only enter the street if you live in the local zone.
Drive at a speed less than 40 km/h if you are not a resident of the local zone.
Not exceed 40 km/h and keep a special lookout for bicycle riders, pedestrians and children.
explain: 40kph is the limit in high pedestrian activity areas, local traffic areas, school zones at prescribed times and school bus blackspot areas.

q: Speed limit signs (such as the one shown) tell drivers -
options: The minimum speed they are allowed to drive.
The recommended speed they are allowed to drive.
The maximum speed they are allowed to drive.
explain: Speed limit signs are always a black number inside a red circle. Exceeding the speed limit by any speed is technically against the law and you can be fined even if you are doing 1kph over the limit.

q: Driving faster than the maximum speed limit is -
options: Never legally permitted.
Permitted only when passing another vehicle.
Only permitted when other vehicles are going faster than the speed limit.
explain: Exceeding the speed limit by any speed is technically against the law and you can be fined even if you are doing 1kph over the limit.

q: It is 9.20am on a school day. You are driving at 60 km/h, the same speed as traffic around you. You pass this sign but the other cars do not slow down much. What should you do?
options: Drive at the speed of the other drivers because it is safer to go with the flow of traffic than slow others up.
Stay at 60 km/h because it is nearly 9.30am and the times on the school sign are only advisory.
Slow down immediately to 40 km/h or less even though other drivers want to go faster.
explain: 40kph is the limit in school zones at prescribed times and school bus blackspot areas.

q: Where there are no speed limit signs, the speed limit is 100 km/h, unless -
options: The road you are driving on is gravel.
There are street lights along the road.
There's an emergency, which mean speed limits don't apply.
explain: If a road has street lights and is urban in the absence of other posted limits it will be 50kph.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Road ahead slippery when wet, drive carefully.
Steep down-grade in the road ahead, slow down.
Road under repair, slow down.
explain: There is a steep hill ahead. You should slow down and change down one or two gears to allow your engine to take over some of the braking. Be careful you don't suffer from 'brake fade' where your brakes stop being effective. If you notice this happening, pull over immediately and let the brakes cool down.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Traffic travels in each direction.
No turns permitted.
Double lane bridge ahead.
explain: This sign means that traffic travels in two directions. You might see it after exiting a motorway or dual carriageway or after a one-way street.

q: You should expect this sign, when -
options: A two lane bridge is ahead, slow down and drive carefully.
A divided road is ahead, prepare for a change in traffic conditions.
Freeway conditions are ahead, maximum speed is 100 km/h.
explain: When the two-way road you are on is about to become a divided road you will see this sign.

q: What does this sign tell you?
options: You are approaching an animal farm.
Animals are crossing the road ahead, stop and wait for directions.
There may be animals on or near the road ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop to avoid collision.
explain: There may be livestock on the road. Slow down and pay special attention to scanning the verges so you can anticipate if livestock might move in front of your vehicle.

q: When you see this sign, what must you do?
options: Drive quickly over the railway crossing.
Stop before the railway crossing, wait for 1 minute and proceed if the crossing is clear.
Slow down and be ready to stop and give way to a train.
explain: This sign indicates there is a railway level crossing with two tracks ahead. You must give way to trains approaching.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Hospital ahead, drive carefully.
Crossroads ahead, reduce your speed and watch out for other traffic and pedestrians.
Cemetery ahead.
explain: This sign is for a crossroads ahead and you may need to give way at the crossroads, depending on the signage.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Vehicles must not stop at the kerb, unless picking up goods.
Vehicles must not stop at the kerb, except if picking up a passenger.
Vehicles are not allowed to stop at the kerb except in a medical emergency.
explain: No stopping signs - you can only stop here if it's a medical emergency.

q: When you see this sign you -
options: Must not stop your vehicle at the kerb during the times shown.
Must not stop here at any time.
May stop at any time to pick up or drop off passengers.
explain: A clearway is a section of road where parking is prohibited during certain times, in this case between 3:30-6:30pm, Monday to Friday.

q: When you see this sign you should -
options: Stop, only if a train is at the crossing.
Slow down, then drive slowly over the crossing looking both ways for trains.
Come to a complete stop, look both ways for trains and proceed with caution if no trains are approaching.
explain: You must always stop at a stop sign.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Stop and help aged pedestrians across the road.
Slow down and look out for pedestrians crossing the road ahead.
Hospital ahead, slow down and proceed with caution.
explain: This area has been identified as one where pedestrians are common and may be crossing the road. It could be near shopping centres or other public amenities.

q: When you see this sign you should -
options: Not drive beyond the sign.
Drive with caution.
Not pass another vehicle.
explain: This no entry sign indicates you cannot drive beyond it as it may be the entrance to an exit-only driveway or a one-way road with traffic coming towards you.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Turn around and go back, you are going the wrong way.
Sharp bend to the right ahead, slow down and drive carefully.
No right turn allowed.
explain: This sign indicates a sharp right hand turn. You may need to slow down, especially if it is wet.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: You must not turn to the left.
You must not turn to the left or the right.
You must not turn to the right.
explain: This sign means you must not turn to the left. This could be to prevent you from turning into a one-way street.

q: When you see this sign you should -
options: Stop in the middle of the railway tracks and look both ways for approaching trains.
Continue at the same speed and not look both ways for approaching trains.
Slow down and be prepared to stop if the lights start flashing, warning you of an approaching train.
explain: This sign indicates there is a railway level crossing with two tracks ahead. Slow down and be prepared to stop if the lights are flashing and give way to approaching trains.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Drive carefully, and watch out for kangaroos entering the road for the next 30 km.
Zoo 30 km ahead.
Nature reserve 30 km ahead.
explain: Advisory signs with distances warn of a hazard and for how long that hazard is in effect. Drive any distance out of the city and you'll probably see something similar to this one which warns of kangaroos on the road for the next 30 km.

q: You are most likely to find this sign, where -
options: There is an athletic field ahead.
Children may be crossing the road ahead, slow down and be prepared to make a safe stop.
Pedestrians are not allowed.
explain: This area may have children present, for example, near a school, play area, or swimming pool. Be careful and be prepared to slow down if necessary. Kids have less road sense and could run out in front of you if distracted by something the other side of the road.

q: When you see this sign you must -
options: Slow down and be prepared to give way to traffic on your right only, if there is any danger of a collision.
Stop and give way to all traffic even if the intersection is clear.
Slow down and be prepared to stop and give way to all traffic if there is any danger of a collision.
explain: Give way: Slow down and be prepared to stop and give way to all traffic if there is any danger of a collision.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: School children crossing the road ahead, prepare to stop.
Traffic controller ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop.
Traffic lights out of order, Police on duty ahead.
explain: If there's a worker or traffic controller with a stop sign directing traffic then you might see this sign. This sign can also be in black and red.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Give way sign ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop.
Cattle or sheep crossing the road ahead, drive slowly.
Railway level crossing ahead, slow down and look out for trains, be prepared to stop.
explain: Advanced warning of an of a railway level crossing ahead.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Trucks must use low gear.
Slow down and beware of trucks entering from the side.
Heavy vehicle checking station ahead.
explain: This sign indicates that trucks may be pulling out from side streets. You may see these signs near industrial areas, for example.

q: When you see this sign, you should -
options: Take a break, rest area ahead.
Take care, trucks crossing the road ahead.
Drive carefully and watch out for traffic entering from a side-road intersection ahead.
explain: You are approaching an intersection and traffic may enter from the side road.

q: You should expect this sign -
options: If a one way street is ahead.
When a divided road ends and two way traffic is ahead.
If a one lane bridge is ahead.
explain: You are currently driving on a divided road and the road will join another road with traffic heading in the opposite direction to form two-way traffic.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Stop, red light camera in operation.
If traffic lights are out of order or the amber light is flashing, you must stop and give way to traffic as if you are at an intersection with stop signs.
Stop at all times and give way to all traffic.
explain: If the lights are not working, or the amber is flashing you treat this intersection like you would any intersection with a stop sign.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: A sharp depression in the road is ahead, be prepared, slow down.
Do not drive with your lights on high beam.
Police station ahead.
explain: A sharp depression in the road can bottom out your suspension in extreme cases if you are going too fast. This can not only damage your car, but could cause you to spin and leave the road. Be prepared to slow down if necessary. It may also conceal other vehicles coming towards you so take care if you want to overtake another vehicle.

q: This sign means you should -
options: Pass to the left of the sign.
Turn left at next street.
Drive carefully, roundabout ahead.
explain: When you see a 'Keep left' sign, you must stay to the left of the sign.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Road may be slippery when wet, slow down and drive carefully.
Sharp turns in the road ahead.
Road under repair, drive carefully.
explain: Slippery when wet. Rain can cause the road to be much more slippery in areas where a high build-up of oil, tyre rubber and road grime occurs, and there is a risk that you might skid if you are going too fast for the conditions. Slow down and take care.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Vehicles may park in this area for up to ten minutes.
Motorcyclists may park in this area.
Only vehicles carrying a disable person and displaying a mobility parking authority may park in this area.
explain: Only vehicles carrying a disable person and displaying a mobility parking authority may park in this area. Other vehicles might be ticketed or towed.

q: When you see this sign you should -
options: Slow down, there is a dangerous curve ahead.
Watch out, the road ahead may be flooded.
Drive carefully, you are reaching the top of the hill and will not be able to see a safe distance in front of you.
explain: There's a crest of a hill ahead. Be careful if you are overtaking as you might not be able to see vehicles coming towards you that are the other side of the crest.

q: You should expect this sign, if -
options: You are approaching a school or playground.
A give way sign at an intersection is ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop.
You are approaching an intersection with traffic lights, be prepared to stop.
explain: Advanced warning of an intersection where you have to give way. The intersection might be concealed. Slow down and be prepared to stop to give way to other traffic.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: No through road ahead, slow down.
Tollway ahead, be prepared to stop and pay toll.
T-intersection ahead. If you are on the terminating road, you must give way to all vehicles approaching from your right or left.
explain: T-intersection ahead. If you are on the terminating road, you must give way to all vehicles approaching from your right or left.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Intersection ahead with traffic lights, prepare to stop.
Railway level crossing with flashing signals ahead, slow down, drive carefully, and be prepared to stop.
Red light camera in use at traffic lights ahead.
explain: Railway level crossing with flashing signals ahead, slow down, drive carefully, and be prepared to stop. The level crossing is usually indicated by one or more signs, most often a crossbuck (a metal cross with railway crossing written on it).

q: What does this sign mean?
options: You are approaching a roundabout, prepare to give way.
Stop sign ahead, slow down and prepare to stop.
One way traffic ahead.
explain: Advanced warning of an intersection where you have to stop. The intersection might be concealed. Be prepared to stop to give way to other traffic.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: No left turn.
One lane bridge ahead, slow down.
You may travel only in the direction in which the arrow is pointing.
explain: You must follow the direction of the sign as it's a one-way street.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Overhead footbridge for pedestrians ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop.
Joggers ahead, drive carefully.
explain: This sign means that there is a pedestrian crossing ahead. Slow down and be prepared to stop.

q: When you see this sign you must -
options: Slow down and be prepared to stop only if there is any danger of a collision with another vehicle or pedestrian.
Stop at the stop line and give way to all traffic on your right only.
Stop at the stop line and give way to all traffic.
explain: Compulsory stop. All vehicles must stop and give way using the give way rules. A stop sign will usually be painted on the road showing you where to stop.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: You must not turn to the right.
You may turn to the right.
You must give way to traffic on your right.
explain: This sign means you must not turn to the right. You might see it to prevent you from turning the wrong way into a one-way street (along with the no entry sign above), or where it would be dangerous for you to make a turn across oncoming traffic.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: You are not to exceed 60 km/h.
You can go faster than 60 km/h.
You are on Highway 60.
explain: Speed limit signs are always a black number inside a red circle. You are not to exceed 60 km/h.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: All traffic must travel in the direction of the arrow.
Follow the arrow unless you are turning right.
Road curves to the left ahead.
explain: Traffic can only proceed in the direction of the arrow, in this case left. This might be seen if the lane only turns to the left.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: You must drive faster than 100 km/h.
You must not drive faster than 100 km/h.
The sign applies to truck drivers only, cars can travel at any speed.
explain: Speed limit signs are always a black number inside a red circle. You are not to exceed 100 km/h.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: This lane is reserved for bicycle riders only.
Motor cars carrying one passenger may use this lane.
Vehicles carrying three or more people, and motorcycles may use this lane.
explain: Between 6am-10am Monday to Friday this transit lane requires that you have at least two passengers in addition to yourself, or you can use it riding a motorbike. Pets are not classed as passengers in a T2 or T3 lane.

q: You are most likely to find this sign -
options: On the approach to a bridge which has room for only two vehicles, slow down and proceed with caution.
When a bridge is not safe to drive on.
If there is a footbridge for pedestrians ahead.
explain: Narrow bridge ahead. Watch for pedestrians on the bridge and wide loads coming towards you that could be too wide for you both to drive across the bridge at the same time. There may also be a supplementary plate indicating who has priority over the bridge.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Bicycle riders not allowed on the roadway.
Watch out for bicycle riders along the roadway or when turning.
You are approaching a children's playground, slow down.
explain: This is an area with more than average bicycles so be vigilant when looking for them as they can be difficult to see.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Children's playground ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop.
Workers ahead, slow down and be prepared to stop.
Do not litter.
explain: Road workers may be working on the road and you may be instructed to stop. This sign might also be in orange. Road repairs can cause the road to be slippery, and you may come around a corner to find a traffic controller with a handheld sign directing traffic, therefore be prepared to stop.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Stop at all times and give way to all traffic on your right.
All traffic must turn back at the roundabout.
Slow down, be ready to stop and give way to all vehicles already on the roundabout if there is a danger of a collision.
explain: There's a roundabout ahead. Give way to your right.

q: What does this sign means?
options: You can overtake vehicles only on the left side.
You must stay in the left lane and must not overtake any vehicles.
You must stay in or move to the left lane, unless you are overtaking another vehicle.
explain: Stay in the left lane unless you need to overtake another vehicle. You will find this sign at the beginning of passing lanes.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Merging traffic, give way to your right.
Form one lane of traffic.
Road narrows ahead, slow down and prepare for a change in traffic conditions.
explain: The road narrows, so be careful, especially of wider vehicles coming in the opposite direction.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: All right lane traffic must turn right at the next intersection.
Right lane traffic may turn right or go straight ahead at the next intersection.
One way traffic ahead.
explain: You must not go straight on from the right lane; you can only turn right.

q: You are most likely to find this sign -
options: As you approach a winding road, slow down and drive with caution.
If there is a steep hill ahead.
If an unsealed road is ahead.
explain: Windy road ahead: there may be bends that are sharper than you anticipate, so the safest way is to slow down. The first curve will be to the right.

q: If the red lights on this sign are flashing what are you required to do?
options: Slow down and drive carefully over the crossing if you cannot see a train approaching.
Stop until red lights stop flashing then drive on if it is safe to do so.
Stop until train has passed then proceed immediately.
explain: If there are lights flashing then you must stop. If a train passes and the lights continue to flash or the barrier doesn't move another train might be coming, so remain where you are.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: Next main town 35 km to the right.
Winding road ahead for next 35 km.
Slow down, the maximum safe speed around the next curve in the road is 35km/h.
explain: There's a curve to the right with an advisory speed of 35kph in dry weather. This would make it quite a sharp curve, so be prepared to slow down, especially if you are a learner driver as there could be other hazards such as wet road markings or gravel in the road.

q: What does this sign mean?
options: The road ahead is closed, go back.
There is a tunnel ahead, turn on your headlights.
There is a hump (sudden slope up and down) in the road ahead, slow down.
explain: There's a road hump or speed bump ahead. Driving too fast over these can damage your suspension.
